H1: A primitive word; father in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application: - chief, (fore-) father ([-less]), X patrimony, principal. Compare names in " Abi-"
H3: From the same as H24; a green plant: - greenness, fruit.
H5: Of foreign origin; Abagtha, a eunuch of Xerxes: - Abagtha.
H6: A primitive root; properly to wander away, that is lose oneself; by implication to perish (causatively, destroy): - break, destroy (-uction), + not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, X and surely, take, be undone, X utterly, be void of, have no way to flee.
H8: Active participle of H6; (concretely) wretched or (abstractly) destruction: - perish.
H9: From H6; concretely something lost ; abstractly destruction, that is Hades: - lost. Compare H10.
H10: The same as H9, miswritten for H11; a perishing: - destruction.
H11: Intensively from H6; abstractly a perishing ; concretely Hades: - destruction.
H14: A primitive root; to breathe after, that is (figuratively) to be acquiescent: - consent, rest content, will, be willing.
H16: From H14 (in the sense of bending towards); the papyrus: - swift.
H17: From H14 (in the sense of desiring); want: - sorrow.
H18: From H75; a manger or stall: - crib.
H19: From an unused root (apparently meaning to turn); brandishing of a sword: - point.
H20: Of uncertain derivation; a melon (only plural): - melon.
H21: From H1; fatherly ; Abi, Hezekiah's mother: - Abi.
H22: From H1 and H410; father (that is possessor) of God ; Abiel, the name of two Israelites: - Abiel.
H23: From H1 and H622; father of gathering (that is gatherer); Abiasaph, an Israelite: - Abiasaph.
H24: From an unused root (meaning to be tender); green, that is a young ear of grain; hence the name of the month Abib or Nisan: - Abib, ear, green ears of corn.
H25: From H1 and H1391; father (that is founder) of Gibon ; Abi-Gibon, perhaps an Israelite: - father of Gibeon.
H26: From H1 and H1524; father (that is source) of joy ; Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses: - Abigal.
H27: From H1 and H1777; father of judgment (that is judge); Abidan, an Israelite: - Abidan.
H28: From H1 and H3045; father of knowledge (that is knowing); Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah: - Abida, Abidah.
H29: From H1 and H3050; father (that is worshipper) of Jah ; Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses: - Abiah, Abijah.
H30: From H1 and H1931; father (that is worshipper) of Him (that is God); Abihu, a son of Aaron: - Abihu.
H31: From H1 and H1935; father (that is, possessor) of renown ; Abihud, the name of two Israelites: - Abihud.
H32: (More correct in its second form); from H1 and H2428; father (that is, possessor) of might ; Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses: - Abihail.
H33: From H44 with the article inserted; father of the Ezrite ; and Abiezrite or descendant of Abiezer: - Abiezrite.
H34: From H14, in the sense of want (especially in feeling); destitute: - beggar, needy, poor (man).
H35: From H14; provocative of desire ; the caper berry (from its stimulative taste): - desire.
H36: From H1 and H2898; father of goodness (that is, good); Abitub, an Israelite: - Abitub.
H37: From H1 and H2919; father of dew (that is, fresh); Abital, a wife of King David: - Abital.
H38: From H1 and H3220; father of (the) sea (that is, seaman); Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah: - Abijam.
H39: From H1 and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe); Abimael, a son of Joktan: - Abimael.
H40: From H1 and H4428; father of (the) king ; Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites: - Abimelech.
H41: From H1 and H5068; father of generosity (that is, liberal); Abinadab, the name of four Israelites: - Abinadab.
H42: From H1 and H5278; father of pleasantness (that is, gracious); Abinoam, an Israelite: - Abinoam.
H43: Construction from H23; Ebjasaph, an Israelite: - Ebiasaph.
H44: From H1 and H5829; father of help (that is, helpful); Abiezer, the name of two Israelites: - Abiezer.
H45: From H1 and an unused root of uncertain derivation; probably father of strength (that is, valiant); Abialbon, an Israelite: - Abialbon.
H46: From H82; mighty (spoken of God): - mighty (one).
H47: For H46: - angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout [-hearted], strong (one), valiant.
H48: From H1 and H7311; father of height (that is, lofty); Abiram, the name of two Israelites: - Abiram.
H49: From H1 and H7686; father of error (that is, blundering); Abishag, a concubine of David: - Abishag.
H50: From H1 and H7171; father of plenty (that is, prosperous); Abishua, the name of two Israelites: - Abishua.
H51: From H1 and H7791; father of (the) wall (that is, perhaps mason), Abishur, an Israelites: - Abishur.
H52: From H1 and H7862; father of a gift (that is, probably generous); Abishai, an Israelite: - Abishai.
H53: From H1 and H7965; father of peace (that is, friendly); Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite: - Abishalom, Absalom.
H54: Contracted from H1 and H3498; father of abundance (that is, liberal); Ebjathar, an Israelite: - Abiathar.
H55: A primitive root; probably to coil upward: - mount up.
H56: A primitive root; to bewail: - lament, mourn.
H58: From an unused root (meaning to be grassy); a meadow : - plain. Compare also the proper names beginning with Abel-.
H59: From H58; a meadow ; Abel, the name of two places in Palestine: - Abel.
H61: Apparently from H56 through the idea of negation ; nay, that is, truly or yet: - but, indeed, nevertheless, verily.
H62: From H58 and H1004 and H4601; meadow of Beth-Maakah ; Abel of Beth-Maakah, a place in Palestine: - Abel-beth-maachah, Abel of Beth-maachah.
H63: From H58 and the plural of H7848, with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias ; Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine: - Abel-shittim.
H64: From H58 and the plural of H3754; meadow of vineyards ; Abel-Keramim, a place in Palestine: - plain of the vineyards.
H65: From H58 and H4246; meadow of dancing ; Abel-Mecholah, a place in Palestine: - Abel-meholah.
H66: From H58 and H4325; meadow of water ; Abel-Majim, a place in Palestine: - Abel-maim.
H67: From H58 and H4714; meadow of Egypt ; Abel-Mitsrajim, a place in Palestine: - Abel-mizraim.
H68: From the root of H1129 through the meaning, to build ; a stone: - + carbuncle, + mason, + plummet, [chalk-, hail-, bead-, sling-] stone (-ny), (divers) weight (-s).
H70: From the same as H68; a pair of stones (only dual); a potter's wheel or a midwife's stool (consisting alike of two horizontal disks with a support between): - wheel, stool.
H71: Perhaps feminine of H68; stony ; Abanah, a river near Damascus: - Abana. Compare H549.
H72: From H68 and H5828 with the article inserted; stone of the help ; Eben ha-Ezer, a place in Palestine: - Ebenezer.
H73: Of uncertain derivation; a belt: - girdle.
H74: From H1 and H5216; father of light (that is, enlightening); Abner, an Israelite: - Abner.
H75: A primitive root; to fodder: - fatted, stalled.
H76: (By reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth); an inflammatory pustule (as eruption): - blains.
H77: From an unused root, probably means to gleam ; conspicuous ; Ebets, a place in Palestine: - Abez.
H78: From the same as H76; splendid ; Ibtsan, an Israelite: - Ibzan.
H79: A primitive root; probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from H80; to bedust, that is, grapple: - wrestle.
H80: From root of H79; light particles (as volatile): - (small) dust, powder.
H82: A primitive root; to soar: - fly.
H85: Contracted from H1 and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude ; Abraham, the later name of Abram: - Abraham.
H86: Probably an Egyptian word meaning kneel: - bow the knee.
H87: Contracted from H48; high father ; Abram, the original name of Abraham: - Abram.
H88: Plural of H178; water skins ; oboth, a place in the Desert: - Oboth.
H89: Of uncertain derivation (compare H90); Age, an Israelite: - Agee.
H90: Of uncertain derivation (compare H89); flame ; Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings: - Agag.
H91: Patrial or patronymic from H90; an Agagite or descendant (subject) of Agag: - Agagite.
H92: Feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to bind); a band, bundle, knot, or arch: - bunch, burden, troop.
H93: Probably of Persian origin; a nut: - nut.
H94: Passive participle of H103; gathered (that is, received among the sages); Agur, a fanciful name of Solomon: - Agur.
H95: From the same as H94; properly something gathered, that is, perhaps a grain or berry ; used only of a small (silver) coin: - piece [of] silver.
H96: From an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops); a reservoir: - drop.
H97: Dual of H96; a double pond ; Eglajim, a place in Moab: - Eglaim.
H98: From an unused root (meaning to collect as water); a marsh ; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds: - pond, pool, standing [water].
H99: Probably from the same as H98 (in the sense of stagnant water); figuratively sad: - pond.
H100: From the same as H98; a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle); by implication a rush (as growing there); collectively a rope of rushes: - bulrush, caldron, hook, rush.
H101: Probably from H5059; a bowl (as pounded out hollow): - basin, cup, goblet.
H102: Probably from H5062 (through the idea of impending); a cover or heap ; that is, (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops: - bands.
H103: A primitive root; to harvest: - gather.
H104: (Chaldee); of Persian origin; an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman): - letter.
H105: Of uncertain derivation; a basin: - charger.
H106: From H1640 (in the sense of grasping); the clenched hand: - fist.
H107: Feminine of H104; an epistle: - letter.
H108: From the same as H181 (in the sense of enveloping); a fog: - mist, vapor.
H109: A primitive root; to languish: - grieve.
H110: Probably from H109 (in the sense of chastisement) and H410; disciplined of God ; Adbeel, a son of Ishmael: - Adbeel.
H111: Probably an orthographical variation for H2301; Adad (or Hadad), an Edomite: - Hadad.
H112: Of uncertain derivation; Iddo, an Israelite: - Iddo.
H113: From an unused root (meaning to rule); sovereign, that is, controller (human or divine): - lord, master, owner. Compare also names beginning with " Adoni-" .
H114: Probably intensive for H113; powerful ; Addon, apparently an Israelite: - Addon.
H115: Dual from H142 (in the sense of eminence); double mound ; Adorajim, a place in Palestine: - Adoraim.
H116: (Chaldee); of uncertain derivation; then (of time): - now, that time, then.
H117: From H142; wide or (generally) large ; figuratively powerful: - excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty (-ier, one), noble, principal, worthy.
H118: Of Persian derivation; Adalja, a son of Haman: - Adalia.
H119: To show blood (in the face), that is, flush or turn rosy: - be (dyed, made) red (ruddy).
H120: From H119; ruddy, that is, a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.): - X another, + hypocrite, + common sort, X low, man (mean, of low degree), person.
H121: The same as H120; Adam, the name of the first man, also of a place in Palestine: - Adam.
H123: From H122; red (see Gen_25:25); Edom, the elder twin-brother of Jacob; hence the region (Idumaea) occuped by him: - Edom, Edomites, Idumea.
H124: From H119; redness, that is, the ruby, garnet, or some other red gem: - sardius.
H126: Contracted for H127; earthy ; Admah, a place near the Dead Sea: - Admah.
H127: From H119; soil (from its general redness): - country, earth, ground, husband [-man] (-ry), land.
H128: The same as H127; Adamah, a place in Palestine: - Adamah.
H129: From H127; earthy ; Adami, a place in Palestine: - Adami.
H130: Patronymic from H123; an Edomite, or descendant from (or inhabitant of) Edom: - Edomite. See H726.
H131: Plural of H121; red spots; Adummim, a pass in Palestine: - Adummim.
H132: From H119; reddish (of the hair or the complexion): - red, ruddy.
H133: Probably of Persian derivation; Admatha, a Persian nobleman: - Admatha.
H134: From the same as H113 (in the sense of strength); a basis (of a building, a column, etc.): - foundation, socket.
H135: Intensive from the same as H134; firm ; Addan, an Israelite: - Addan.
H136: An emphatic form of H113; the Lord (used as a proper name of God only): - (my) Lord.
H137: From H113 and H966; lord of Bezek ; Adoni-Bezek, a Canaanitish king: - Adoni-bezek.
H138: From H113 and H3050; lord (that is, worshipper) of Jah; Adonijah, the name of three Israelites: - Adonijah.
H139: From H113 and H6664; lord of justice ; Adoni-Tsedek, a Canaanitish king: - Adonizedec.
H140: From H113 and H6965; lord of rising (that is, high); Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites: - Adonikam
H141: From H113 and H7311; lord of height ; Adoniram, an Israelite: - Adoniram.
H142: A primitive root; to expand, that is, be great or (figuratively) magnificent: - (become) glorious, honourable.
H143: Probably of foreign derivation; perhaps meaning fire ; Adar, the H12 th Hebrew month: - Adar.
H145: From H142; amplitude, that is, (concretely) a mantle ; also (figuratively) splendor: - goodly, robe.
H146: Intensive from H142; ample ; Addar, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite: - Addar.
H147: (Chaldee); intensive from a root corresponding to H142; ample, that is, a threshing-floor: - threshingfloor.
H148: (Chaldee); from the same as H147, and H1505; a chief diviner, or astrologer: - judge.
H149: (Chaldee); probably of Persian origin; quickly or carefully: - dilligently.
H150: Of Persian origin; a daric or Persian coin: - dram.
H151: Contracted for H141; Adoram (or Adoniram), an Israelite: - Adoram.
H152: From H142 and H4428; splendor of (the) king ; Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib: - Adrammelech.
H153: (Chaldee); an orthographical variation for H1872; an arm, that is, (figuratively) power: - force.
H154: From the equivalent of H153; mighty ; Edrei, the name of two places in Palestine: - Edrei.
H155: Feminine of H117; something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress); also the same as H145: - garment, glory, goodly, mantle, robe.
H156: A primitive root; to tread out (grain): - thresh.
H157: A primitive root; to have affection for (sexually or otherwise): - (be-) love (-d, -ly, -r), like, friend.
H158: From H157; affection (in a good or a bad sense): - love (-r).
H159: From H156; meaning the same as H158: - love.
H160: Feminine of H158 and meaning the same: - love.
H161: From an unused root meaning to be united ; unity ; Ohad, an Israelite: - Ohad.
H162: Apparently a primitive word expressing pain exclamatorily; Oh !: - ah, alas.
H163: Probably of foreign origin; Ahava, a river of Babylonia: - Ahava.
H164: From the same as H161; united ; Ehud, the name of two or three Israelite: - Ehud.
H165: Apparently an orthographical variation for H346; where. (Used in Hos_13:10, Hos_13:14). " I will be" is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form from H1961: - I will be (Hos_13:10, Hos_13:14) [which is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form from H1961].
H166: A primitive root; to be clear: - shine.
H167: A denominative from H168; to tent: - pitch (remove) a tent.
H168: From H166; a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance): - covering, (dwelling) (place), home, tabernacle, tent.
H169: The same as H168; Ohel, an Israelite: - Ohel.
H170: The first form is in form a feminine of H168, but is in fact for the second form; from H168; her tent (that is, idolatrous sanctuary); Oholah, a symbolic name for Samaria: - Aholah.
H171: From H168 and H1; tent of (his) father ; Oholiab, an Israelite: - Aholiab.
H172: (As with H170 the first form is in form a feminine of H168, but is in fact for the second form); from H168; my tent (is) in her ; Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah: - Aholibah.
H173: From H168 and H1116; tent of (the) height ; Oholibamah, a wife of Esau: - Aholibamah.
H174: (The second form, which is feminine, is used only in the plural); of foreign origin; aloe wood (that is, sticks): - (tree of lign-) aloes.
H175: Of uncertain derivation; Aharon, the brother of Moses: - Aaron.
H176: The first form is presumed to be the " constructive" or genitival form of the second form which is short for H185; desire (and so probably in Pro_31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if: - also, and, either, if, at the least, X nor, or, otherwise, then, whether.
H177: From H176 and H410; wish of God ; Uel, an Israelite: - Uel.
H178: From the same as H1 (apparently through the idea of prattling a father's name); properly a mumble, that is, a water skin (from its hollow sound); hence a necromancer (ventriloquist, as from a jar): - bottle, familiar spirit.
H179: Probably from H56; mournful ; Obil, an Ishmaelite: - Obil.
H180: From H2986 (in the sense of H2988); a stream: - river.
H181: From an unused root meaning to rake together; a poker (for turning or gathering embers): - (fire-) brand.
H182: From the same as H181; turnings (that is, occasions); (adverbially) on account of: - (be-) cause, concerning, sake.
H183: A primitive root; to wish for: - covet, (greatly) desire, be desirous, long, lust (after).
H184: A primitive root; to extend or mark out: - point out.
H185: From H183; longing: - desire, lust after, pleasure.
H186: Perhaps by permutation for H5813, strong ; Uzai, an Israelite: - Uzai.
H187: Of uncertain derivation; Uzal, a son of Joktan: - Uzal.
H188: Probably from H183 (in the sense of crying out after); lamentation ; also interjectionally, Oh !: - alas, woe.
H189: Probably from H183; desirous ; Evi, a Midianitish chief: - Evi.
H191: From an unused root (meaning to be perverse); (figuratively) silly: - fool (-ish) (man).
H192: Of Chaldee derivation and probably meaning soldier of Merodak ; Evil-Merodak, a Babylonian king: - Evil-merodach.
H193: From an unused root meaning to twist, that is, (by implication) be strong ; the body (as being rolled together) also powerful: - mighty, strength.
H194: From H176; if not ; hence perhaps: - if so be, may be, peradventure, unless.
H195: Of Persian derivation; the Ulai (or Eulaeus), a river of Persia: - Ulai.
H196: From H191; silly, foolish ; hence (morally) impious: - foolish.
H197: From H481 (in the sense of tying); a vestibule (as bound to the building): - porch.
H198: Apparently from H481 (in the sense of dumbness); solitary ; Ulam, the name of two Israelites: - Ulam.
H199: Apparently a variation of H194; however or on the contrary: - as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore.
H200: From the same as H191; silliness: - folly, foolishly (-ness).
H201: From H559; talkative ; Omar, a grandson of Esau: - Omar.
H202: Probably from the same as H205 (in the sense of effort, but successful); ability, power, (figuratively) wealth: - force, goods, might, strength, substance.
H203: The same as H202; On, an Israelite: - On.
H204: Of Egyptian derivation; On, a city of Egypt: - On.
H205: From an unused root perhaps meaning properly to pant (hence to exert oneself, usually in vain; to come to naught); strictly nothingness ; also trouble, vanity, wickedness ; specifically an idol : - affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners (-ing), naught, sorrow, unjust, unrighteous, vain, vanity, wicked (-ness.) Compare H369.
H206: The same as H205; idolatry ; Aven, the contemptuous synonym of three places, one in Coele Syria, one in Egypt (On), and one in Palestine (Bethel): - Aven. See also H204, H1007.
H207: From H202; strong ; Ono, a place in Palestine: - Ono.
H208: A variation of H209; strong ; Onam, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite: - Onam.
H209: A variation of H207; strong ; Onan, a son of Judah: - Onan.
H210: Perhaps a corruption of H211; Uphaz, a famous gold region: - Uphaz.
H211: Of uncertain derivation; Ophir, the name of a son of Joktan, and of a gold region in the East: - Ophir.
H212: From an unused root meaning to revolve ; a wheel: - wheel.
H213: A primitive root; to press ; (by implication) to be close, hurry, withdraw: - (make) haste (-n, -y), labor, be narrow.
H214: From H686; a depository: - armory, cellar, garner, store(-house), treasure (-house) (-y).
H215: A primitive root; to be (causatively make) luminous (literally and metaphorically): - X break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire, shine.
H216: From H215; illumination or (concretely) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.): - bright, clear, + day, light (-ning), morning, sun.
H217: From H215; flame, hence (in the plural) the East (as being the region of light): - fire, light. See also H224.
H218: The same as H217; Ur, a place in Chaldaea; also an Israelite: - Ur.
H219: Feminine of H216; luminousness, that is, (figuratively) prosperity ; also a plant (as being bright): - herb light.
H220: By transposition for H723; a stall: - cote.
H221: From H217; fiery ; Uri, the name of three Israelites: - Uri.
H222: From H217 and H410; flame of God ; Uriel, the name of two Israelites: - Uriel.
H223: From H217 and H3050; flame of Jah ; Urijah, the name of one Hittite and five Israelites: - Uriah, Urijah.
H224: Plural of H217; lights ; Urim, the oracular brilliancy of the figures in the high priest's breastplate: - Urim.
H225: A primitive root; properly to come, that is, (impliedly) to assent: - consent.
H226: Probably from H225 (in the sense of appearing); a signal (literally or figuratively), as a flag, beacon, monument, omen, prodigy, evidence, etc.: - mark, miracle, (en-) sign, token.
H227: A demonstrative adverb; at that time or place ; also as a conjugation, therefore: - beginning, for, from, hitherto, now, of old, once, since, then, at which time, yet.
H228: (Chaldee); to kindle ; (by implication) to heat: - heat, hot.
H229: Probably from H231; hyssop like ; Ezbai, an Israelite: - Ezbai.
H230: (Chaldee); of uncertain derivation; firm: - be gone.
H231: Probably of foreign derivation; hyssop: - hyssop.
H232: From H246; something girt ; a belt, also a band: - girdle.
H233: Probably from H227; at that time: - then.
H234: From H2142; a reminder ; specifically remembrance offering: - memorial.
H235: A primitive root; to go away, hence to disappear: - fail, gad about, go to and fro [but in Eze_27:19 the word is rendered by many " from Uzal," by others " yarn" ], be gone (spent).
H236: (Chaldee); the same as H235; to depart: - go (up).
H237: From H235; departure ; ezel, a memorial stone in Palestine: - Ezel.
H238: A primitive root; probably to expand ; but used only as a denominative from H241; to broaden out the ear (with the hand), that is, (by implication) to listen: - give (perceive by the) ear, hear (-ken). See H239.
H239: A primitive root (rather identical with H238 through the idea of scales as if two ears); to weigh, that is, (figuratively) ponder: - give good heed.
H240: From H238; a spade or paddle (as having a broad end): - weapon.
H241: From H238; broadness, that is, (concretely) the ear (from its form in man): - + advertise, audience, + displease, ear, hearing, + show.
H242: From H238 and H7609; plat of Sheerah (that is, settled by him); Uzzen Sheerah, a place in Palestine: - Uzzen-sherah.
H243: From H238 and H8396; flats (that is, tops) of Tabor (that is, situated on it); aznoth Tabor, a place in Palestine: - Aznoth-tabor.
H244: From H241; having (quick) ears ; Ozni, an Israelite; also an Oznite (collectively), his descendants: - Ozni, Oznites.
H245: From H238 and H3050; heard by Jah ; Azanjah, an Israelite: - Azaniah.
H246: A variation for H2131; manacles: - chains.
H247: A primitive root; to belt: - bind (compass) about, gird (up, with).
H248: A variation for H2220; the arm: - arm.
H249: From H2224 (in the sense of springing up); a spontaneous growth, that is, native (tree or persons): - bay tree, (home-) born (in the land), of the (one's own) country (nation).
H250: Patronymic from H2246; an Ezrachite or descendants of Zerach: - Ezrahite.
H251: A primitive word; a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like H1)): - another, brother (-ly), kindred, like, other. Compare also the proper names beginning with " Ah-" or " Ahi-" .
H253: A variation for H162; Oh ! (expressive of grief or surprise): - ah, alas.
H254: Of uncertain derivation; a fire pot or chafing dish: - hearth.
H255: Probably from H253; a howler or lonesome wild animal: - doleful creature.
H256: The second form used once (by contraction) in Jer_29:22; from H251 and H1; brother (that is, friend) of (his) father ; Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon: - Ahab.

H502: A primitive root, to associate with; hence to learn (and causatively to teach): - learn, teach, utter.
H503: Denominative from H505; causatively to make a thousandfold: - bring forth thousands.
H504: From H502; a family ; also (from the sense of yoking or taming) an ox or cow: - family, kine, oxen.
H505: Properly the same as H504; hence (an ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand: - thousand.
H507: The same as H505; Eleph, a place in Palestine: - Eleph.
H508: From H410 and H6466; God (is) act ; Elpaal, an Israelite: - Elpaal.
H509: A primitive root; to press: - urge.
H510: Probably from H408 and H6965; a non-rising (that is, resistlessness): - no rising up.
H511: From H410 and H7069; God has obtained ; Elkanah, the name of seven Israelites: - Elkanah.
H512: Patrial from a name of uncertain derivation; an Elkoshite or native of Elkosh: - Elkoshite.
H513: Probably from H410 and a masculine form of H8435 (compare H8434); God (is) generator ; Eltolad, a place in Palestine: - Eltolad.
H514: Of uncertain derivation; Eltekeh or Elteke, a place in Palestine: - Eltekeh.
H515: From H410 and H8626; God (is) straight ; Eltekon, a place in Palestine: - Eltekon.
H516: From H408 and H7843; Thou must not destroy ; probably the opening words of a popular song: - Al-taschith.
H517: A primitive word; a mother (as the bond of the family); in a wide sense (both literally and figuratively); (like H1): - dam, mother, X parting.
H518: A primitive particle; used very widely as demonstrative, lo !; interrogitive, whether ?; or conditional, if, although ; also Oh that !, when ; hence as a negative, not: - (and, can-, doubtless, if, that) (not), + but, either, + except, + more (-over if, than), neither, nevertheless, nor, oh that, or, + save (only, -ing), seeing, since, sith, + surely (no more, none, not), though, + of a truth, + unless, + verily, when, whereas, whether, while, + yet.
H519: Apparently a primitive word; a maidservant or female slave: - (hand-) bondmaid (-woman,) maid (-servant).
H520: Prolonged from H517; properly a mother (that is, unit) of measure, or the forearm (below the elbow), that is, a cubit ; also a door base (as a bond of the entrance): - cubit, + hundred [by exchange for H3967], measure, post.
H522: The same as H520; Ammah, a hill in Palestine: - Ammah.
H523: From the same as H517; a collection, that is, community of persons: - nation, people.
H525: From H539, probably in the sense of training ; skilled, that is, an architect (like H542): - one brought up.
H526: The same as H525; Amon, the name of three Israelites: - Amon.
H527: A variation for H1995; a throng of people: - multitude.
H528: Of Egyptian derivation; Amon (that is, Ammon or Amn), a deity of Egypt (used only as an adjunct of H4996): - multitude, populous.
H529: From H539; established, that is, (figuratively) trusty ; also (abstractly) trustworthiness: - faith (-ful), truth.
H530: Feminine of H529; literally firmness ; figuratively security ; moral fidelity: - faith (-ful, -ly, -ness, [man]), set office, stability, steady, truly, truth, verily.
H531: From H553; strong ; Amots, an Israelite: - Amoz.
H532: An abbreviated for H526; Ami, an Israelite: - Ami.
H533: From H553; strong or (abstractly) strength: - courageous, mighty, strong (one).
H534: Apparently from H559 (in the sense of self exaltation); a summit (of a tree or mountain): - bough, branch.
H535: A primitive root; to droop ; by implication to be sick, to mourn: - languish, be weak, wax feeble.
H538: From H517; gathering spot; Amam, a place in Palestine: - Amam.
H539: A primitive root; properly to build up or support ; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain; once (in Isa_30:21; by interchange for H541) to go to the right hand: - hence assurance, believe, bring up, establish, + fail, be faithful (of long continuance, stedfast, sure, surely, trusty, verified), nurse, (-ing father), (put), trust, turn to the right.
H540: (Chaldee); corresponding to H539: - believe, faithful, sure.
H541: Denominative from H3225; to take the right hand road: - turn to the right. See H539.
H542: From H539 (in the sense of training); an expert: - cunning workman.
H543: From H539; sure ; abstractly faithfulness ; adverbially truly: - Amen, so be it, truth.
H545: Feminine of H544 (in the specific sense of training); tutelage: - brought up.
H546: Feminine of H544 (in its usual sense); adverbially surely: - indeed.
H547: Feminine active participle of H544 (in the original sense of supporting); a column: - pillar.
H548: Feminine of H543; something fixed, that is, a covenant, an allowance: - certain portion, sure.
H549: The same as H548; Amanah, a mountain near Damascus: - Amana.
H550: From H539; faithful ; Amnon (or Aminon), a son of David: - Amnon.
H551: Adverb from H544; verily: - indeed, no doubt, surely, (it is, of a) true (-ly, -th).
H552: An orthographical variation of H551: - in (very) deed; of a surety.
H553: A primitive root; to be alert, physically (on foot) or mentally (in courage): - confirm, be courageous (of good courage, stedfastly minded, strong, stronger), establish, fortify, harden, increase, prevail, strengthen (self), make strong (obstinate, speed).
H554: Probably from H553; of a strong color, that is, red (others fleet): - bay.
H557: From H553; strong ; Amtsi, an Israelite: - Amzi.
H558: From H553 and H3050; strength of Jah ; Amatsjah, the name of four Israelites: - Amaziah.
H559: A primitive root; to say (used with great latitude): - answer, appoint, avouch, bid, boast self, call, certify, challenge, charge, + (at the, give) command (ment), commune, consider, declare, demand, X desire, determine, X expressly, X indeed, X intend, name, X plainly, promise, publish, report, require, say, speak (against, of), X still, X suppose, talk, tell, term, X that is, X think, use [speech], utter, X verily, X yet.
H560: (Chaldee); corresponding to H559: - command, declare, say, speak, tell.
H561: From H559; something said: - answer, X appointed unto him, saying, speech, word.
H562: The same as H561: - promise, speech, thing, word.
H563: (Chaldee); perhaps from H560 (in the sense of bringing forth); a lamb: - lamb.
H564: From H559; talkative ; Immer, the name of five Israelites: - Immer.
H565: The second form is the feminine of H561, and meaning the same: - commandment, speech, word.
H566: From H564; wordy ; Imri, the name of two Israelites: - Imri.
H567: Probably a patronymic from an unused name derived from H559 in the sense of publicity, that is, prominence; thus a mountaineer ; an Emorite, one of the Canaanitish tribes: - Amorite.
H568: From H559 and H3050; Jah has said (that is, promised); Amarjah, the name of nine Israelites: - Amariah.
H569: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; Amraphel, a king of Shinar: - Amraphel.
H570: Time past, that is, yesterday or last night: - former time, yesterday (-night).
H571: Contracted from H539; stability ; figuratively certainty, truth, trustworthiness: - assured (-ly), establishment, faithful, right, sure, true (-ly, -th), verity.
H572: From H4969; properly something expansive, that is, a bag: - sack.
H573: From H571; veracious ; Amittai, an Israelite: - Amittai.
H574: (Chaldee); from a root corresponding to that of H4975; well loined (that is, burly) or mighty: - terrible.
H575: Contracted from H370; where ?; hence whither ?, when ?; also hither and thither: - + any (no) whither, now, where, whither (-soever).
H576: (Chaldee); corresponding to H589; I: - I, as for me.
H577: Apparently contracted from H160 and H4994: oh now! : - I (me) beseech (pray) thee, O.
H578: A primitive root; to groan: - lament, mourn.
H579: A primitive root (perhaps rather identical with H578 through the idea of contraction in anguish); to approach ; hence to meet in various senses: - befall, deliver, happen, seek a quarrel.
H581: (Chaldee); the second form is the feminine of the first form; corresponding to H1992; they: - X are, them, these.
H582: From H605; properly a mortal (and thus differeing from the more dignified H120); hence a man in general (singly or collectively). It is often unexpressed in the English Version, especially when used in apposition with another word: - another, X [blood-] thirsty, certain, chap [-man], divers, fellow, X in the flower of their age, husband, (certain, mortal) man, people, person, servant, some (X of them), + stranger, those, + their trade. It is often unexpressed in the Engl. version, especially when used in apposition with another word. Compare H376.
H583: The same as H582; Enosh, a son of Seth: - Enos.
H584: A primitive root; to sigh: - groan, mourn, sigh.
H585: From H584; sighing: - groaning, mourn, sigh.
H587: Apparently from H595; we: - ourselves, us, we.
H588: Probably from the same root as H5170; a gorge or narrow pass; Anacharath, a place in Palestine: - Anaharath.
H589: Contracted from H595; I: - I, (as for) me, mine, myself, we, X which, X who.
H590: Probably from H479 (in the sense of conveyance); a ship or (collectively) a fleet: - galley, navy (of ships).
H591: Feminine of H590; a ship: - ship ([-men]).
H593: From H578 and H5971; groaning of (the) people ; Aniam, an Israelite: - Aniam.
H594: Probably from an unused root meaning to be narrow ; according to most a plumb line, and to others a hook: - plumb-line.
H595: A primitive pronoun; I: - I, me, X which.
H596: A primitive root; to mourn, that is, complain: - complain.
H598: (Chaldee); corresponding to H597; figuratively to distress: - trouble.
H599: A primitive root; to breathe hard, that is, be enraged: - be angry (displeased).
H600: (Chaldee); corresponding to H639 (only in the plural as a singular); the face: - face, visage.
H601: From H599; an unclean bird, perhaps the parrot (from its irascibility): - heron.
H602: A primitive root; to shriek: - cry, groan.
H603: From H602; shrieking: - crying out, groaning, sighing.
H604: The same as H603; some kind of lizard, probably the gecko (from its wail): - ferret.
H605: A primitive root; to be frail, feeble, or (figuratively) melancholy: - desperate (-ly wicked), incurable, sick, woeful.
H606: (Chaldee); corresponding to H582; a man: - man, + whosoever.
H607: (Chaldee); corresponding to H859; thou: - as for thee, thou.
H609: Of uncertain derivation; Asa, the name of a king and of a Levite: - Asa.
H610: From H5480; anointed, that is, an oil flask: - pot.
H612: From H631; a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner): - band, + prison.
H614: From H622; gathered, that is, (abstractly) a gathering in of crops: - ingathering.
H615: From H631; bound, that is, a captive: - (those which are) bound, prisoner.
H617: The same as H616; prisoner ; Assir, the name of two Israelites: - Assir.
H618: From an unused root meaning to heap together; a storehouse (only in the plural): - barn, storehouse.
H619: Of uncertain derivation; Asnah, one of the Nethinim: - Asnah.
H620: Of foreign derivation; Osnappar, an Assyrian king: - Asnapper.
H621: Of Egyptian derivation; Asenath, the wife of Joseph: - Asenath.
H622: A primitive root; to gather for any purpose; hence to receive, take away, that is, remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.): - assemble, bring, consume, destroy, fetch, gather (in, together, up again), X generally, get (him), lose, put all together, receive, recover [another from leprosy], (be) rereward, X surely, take (away, into, up), X utterly, withdraw.
H623: From H622; collector ; Asaph, the name of three Israelites, and of the family of the first: - Asaph.
H624: Passive participle of H622; collected (only in the plural), that is, a collection (of offerings): - threshold, Asuppim.
H625: From H622; a collection (of fruits): - gathering.
H626: From H622; a collection of people (only adverbially): - X together.
H627: Feminine of H624; a collection of (learned) men (only in the plural): - assembly.
H628: By reduplication from H624; gathered up together, that is, a promiscuous assemblage (of people): - mixt multitude.
H629: (Chaldee); of Persian derivation; diligently: - fast, forthwith, speed (-ily)
H630: Of Persian derivation; Aspatha, a son of Haman: - Aspatha.
H631: A primitive root; to yoke or hitch ; by analogy to fasten in any sense, to join battle: - bind, fast, gird, harness, hold, keep, make ready, order, prepare, prison (-er), put in bonds, set in array, tie.
H632: From H631; an obligation or vow (of abstinence): - binding, bond.
H633: (Chaldee); corresponding to H632 in a legal sense; an interdict: - decree.
H634: Of foreign derivation; Esarchaddon, an Assyrian king: - Esar-haddon.
H635: Of Persian derivation; Ester, the Jewish heroine: - Esther.
H636: (Chaldee); corresponding to H6086; a tree or wood: - timber, wood.
H637: A primitive particle; meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjugation); also or yea ; adversatively though: - also, + although, and (furthermore, yet), but, even, + how much less (more, rather than), moreover, with, yea.
H639: From H599; properly the nose or nostril ; hence the face, and occasionally a person ; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire: - anger (-gry), + before, countenance, face, + forbearing, forehead, + [long-] suffering, nose, nostril, snout, X worthy, wrath.
H640: A primitive root (rather a denominative from H636); to gird on (the ephod): - bind, gird.
H641: The same as H646 shortened; Ephod, an Israelite: - Ephod.
H642: Feminine of H646; a girding on (of the ephod); hence generally a plating (of metal): - ephod, ornament.
H643: Apparently of foreign derivation; a pavilion or palace tent: - palace.
H644: A primitive root; to cook, especially to bake: - bake, (-r, [-meats]).
H645: From H6311; strictly a demonstrative particle, here ; but used of time, now or then: - here, now, where?
H646: Second form is a rare form; probably of foreign derivation; a girdle ; specifically the ephod or high priest's shoulder piece; also generally an image: - ephod.
H647: Perhaps from H6315; breeze ; Aphiach, an Israelite: - Aphiah.
H648: From the same as H651 (in the sense of weakness); unripe: - not grown up.
H649: Dual of H639; two nostrils ; Appajim, an Israelite: - Appaim.
H650: From H622; properly containing, that is, a tube ; also a bed or valley of a stream; also a strong thing or a hero: - brook, channel, mighty, river, + scale, stream, strong piece.
H651: From an unused root meaning to set as the sun; dusky: - very dark.
H652: From the same as H651; dusk: - darkness, obscurity, privily.
H653: Feminine of H651; duskiness, figuratively misfortune ; concretely concealment: - dark, darkness, gloominess, X thick.
H654: From H6419; judge ; Ephlal, an Israelite: - Ephlal.
H655: From an unused root meaning to revolve ; a turn, that is, a season: - + fitly.
H656: A primitive root; to disappear, that is, cease: - be clean gone (at an end, brought to nought), fail.
H657: From H656; cessation, that is, an end (especially of the earth); often used adverbially no further ; also (like H6466) the ankle (in the dual), as being the extremity of the leg or foot: - ankle, but (only), end, howbeit, less than nothing, nevertheless (where), no, none (beside), not (any, -withstanding), thing of nought, save (-ing), there, uttermost part, want, without (cause).
H658: From H657 and the plural of H1818; boundary of blood drops; Ephes-Dammim, a place in Palestine: - Ephes-dammim.
H659: From an unused root probably meaning to breathe ; properly a breath, that is, nothing: - of nought.
H660: From H659 (in the sense of hissing); an asp or other venomous serpent: - viper.
H661: A primitive root; to surround: - compassive
H662: A primitive root; to contain, that is, (reflexively) abstain: - force (oneself), restrain.
H663: From H662 (in the sense of strength); fortress ; Aphek (or Aphik), the name of three places in Palestine: - Aphek, Aphik.
H664: Feminine of H663; fortress ; Aphekah, a place in Palestine: - Aphekah.
H665: From an unused root meaning to bestrew ; ashes: - ashes.
H666: From the same as H665 (in the sense of covering); a turban: - ashes.
H667: From H6524 (in the sense of bursting the shell); the brood of a bird: - young (one).
H668: Probably of Egyptian derivation; a palanquin: - chariot.
H669: Dual of a masculine form of H672; double fruit ; Ephrajim, a son of Joseph; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory: - Ephraim Ephraimites
H670: (Chaldee); of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apharesite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria: - Apharsite.
H671: (Chaldee); of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe: - Apharsachites, Apharsathchites.
H672: From H6509; fruitfulness ; Ephrath, another name for Bethlehem; once used in Psa_132:6 perhaps for Ephraim ; also of an Israelitish woman: - Ephrath, Ephratah.
H673: Patrial from H672; an Ephrathite or an Ephraimite: - Ephraimite, Ephrathite.
H674: (Chaldee); of Persian origin; revenue ; others at the last: - revenue.
H675: Of uncertain derivation; Etsbon, the name of two Israelites: - Ezbon.
H676: From the same as H6648 (in the sense of grasping); some thing to seize with, that is, a finger ; by analogy a toe: - finger, toe.
H678: From H680 (in its secondary sense of separation); an extremity (Isa_41:9), also a noble: - chief man, noble.
H679: From H680 (in its primary sense of uniting); a joint of the hand (that is, knuckle); also (according to some) a partywall (Eze_41:8): - [arm] hole, great.
H680: A primitive root; properly to join ; used only as a denominative from H681; to separate ; hence to select, refuse, contract : - keep, reserve, straiten, take.
H681: From H680 (in the sense of joining); a side ; (as a preposition) near : - at, (hard) by, (from) (beside), near (unto), toward, with. See also H1018.
H682: From H680; noble ; Atsel, the name of an Israelite, and of a place in Palestine: - Azal, Azel.
H683: From H680 and H3050 prolonged; Jah has reserved ; Atsaljah, an Israelite: - Azaliah.
H684: From an unused root probably meaning to be strong ; strength (that is, strong); Otsem, the name of two Israelites: - Ozem.
H685: A variation from H6807; properly a step chain ; by analogy a bracelet: - bracelet, chain.
H686: A primitive root; to store up: - (lay up in ) store, (make) treasure (-r).
H687: From H686; treasure ; Etser, an Idumaean: - Ezer.
H688: From H6916; burning, that is, a carbuncle or other fiery gem: - carbuncle.
H689: Probably from H602; slender, that is, the ibex: - wild goat.
H690: Probably for H738; lion ; Ara, an Israelite: - Ara.
H691: Probably for H739; a hero (collectively): - valiant one.
H692: From H691; heroic ; Areli (or an Arelite, collectively), an Israelite and his descendants: - Areli, Arelites.
H693: A primitive root; to lurk: - (lie in) ambush (-ment), lay (lie in) wait.
H694: From H693; ambush ; Arab, a place in Palestine: - Arab.
H695: From H693; ambuscade: - den, lie in wait.
H697: From H7235; a locust (from its rapid increase): - grasshopper, locust.
H698: Feminine of H696 (only in the plural); ambuscades: - spoils.
H699: Feminine participle passive of H693 (as if for lurking); a lattice ; (by implication) a window, dove cot (because of the pigeon holes), chimney (with its apertures for smoke), sluice (with openings for water): - chimney, window.
H700: Plural of H699; Arubboth, a place in Palestine: - Aruboth.
H701: Patrial from H694; an Arbite or native of Arab: - Arbite.
H702: The second form is the masculine form; from H7251; four: - four.
H704: The same as H702; Arba, one of the Anakim: - Arba.
H707: A primitive root; to plait or weave: - weaver (-r).
H708: From H707; a weaving ; a braid ; also a shuttle: - beam, weaver's shuttle.
H709: From the same as H7263; stony ; Argob, a district of Palestine: - Argob.
H710: A variation for H713; purple: - purple.
H712: Perhaps from H7264 (in the sense of being suspended); a box (as a pannier): - coffer.
H713: Of foreign origin; purple (the color or the dyed stuff): - purple.
H714: From an unused root probably meaning to wander ; fugitive ; Ard, the name of two Israelites: - Ard.
H715: From the same as H714; roaming ; Ardon, an Israelite: - Ardon.
H716: Patronymic from H714; an Ardite (collectively) or descendant of Ard: - Ardites.
H717: A primitive root; to pluck: - gather, pluck.
H718: (Chaldee); probably akin to H431; lo! : - behold, lo.
H719: Probably from H7300; a refuge for the roving ; Arvad, an island city of Palestine: - Arvad.
H720: An orthographical variation of H719; fugitive ; Arod, an Israelite: - Arod.
H721: Patrial from H719; an Arvadite or citizen of Arvad: - Arvadite.
H722: Patronymic from H721; an Arodite or descendant of Arod: - Arodi, Arodites.
H723: From H717 (in the sense of feeding); a herding place for an animal: - stall.
H724: Feminine passive participle of H748 (in the sense of restoring to soundness); wholeness (literally or figuratively): - health, made up, perfected.
H725: A variation of H7316; height ; Arumah, a place in Palestine: - Arumah.
H726: A clerical error for H130; an Edomite: - Syrian.
H727: From H717 (in the sense of gathering); a box: - ark, chest, coffin.
H728: All forms by orthographical variation for H711; Aravnah (or Arnijah or Ornah), a Jebusite: - Araunah.
H729: A primitive root; to be firm ; used only in the passive participle as a denominative from H730; of cedar: - made of cedar.
H730: From H729; a cedar tree (from the tenacity of its roots): - cedar (tree).
H731: Feminine of H730; cedar wainscoting: - cedar work.
H732: A primitive root; to travel: - go, wayfaring (man).
H733: From H732; wayfaring ; Arach, the name of three Israelites: - Arah.
H734: From H732; a well trodden road (literally or figuratively); also a caravan: - manner, path, race, rank, traveller, troop, [by-, high-] way.
H735: (Chaldee); corresponding to H734; a road: - way.
H736: Feminine active participle of H732; a caravan: - (travelling) company.
H737: Feminine passive participle of H732 (in the sense of appointing); a ration of food: - allowance, diet, dinner, victuals.
H738: From H717 (in the sense of violence); a lion: - (young) lion, + pierce [from the margin].
H739: From H738 and H410; lion of God, that is, heroic: - lionlike men.
H740: The same as H739; Ariel, a symbolical name for Jerusalem, also the name of an Israelite: - Ariel.
H741: Either by transposition for H739 or more probable, an orthographical variation for H2025; the altar of the Temple: - altar.
H742: Of Persian origin; Aridai, a son of Haman: - Aridai.
H743: Of Persian origin; Aridatha, a son of Haman: - Aridatha.
H745: The same as H738; lion ; Arjeh, an Israelite: - Arieh.
H746: Of foreign origin; Arjok, the name of two Babylonians: - Arioch.
H747: Of Persian origin; Arisai, a son of Haman: - Arisai.
H748: A primitive root; to be (causatively make) long (literally or figuratively): - defer, draw out, lengthen, (be, become, make, pro-) long, + (out-, over-) live, tarry (long).
H749: (Chaldee); properly corresponding to H748, but used only in the sense of reaching to a given point; to suit: - be meet.
H750: From H748; long: - long [-suffering, -winged], patient, slow [to anger].
H751: From H748; length ; Erek, a place in Babylon: - Erech.
H753: From H748; length: - + for ever, length, long.
H755: (Chaldee); from an unused root corresponding to H7392 (in the sense of bending the knee); the knee: - knee.
H756: (Chaldee); patrial from H751; an Arkevite (collectively) or native of Erek: - Archevite.
H757: Patrial from another place (in Palestine) of similar name with H751; an Arkite or native of Erek: - Archi, Archite.
H758: From the same as H759; the highland ; Aram or Syria, and its inhabitants; also the name of a son of Shem, a grandson of Nahor, and of an Israelite: - Aram, Mesopotamia, Syria, Syrians.
H759: From an unused root (meaning to be elevated); a citadel (from its height): - castle, palace. Compare H2038.
H760: From H758 and H6678; Aram of Tsoba (or Coele-syria): - Aram-zobah.
H761: Patrial from H758; an Aramite or Aramaean: - Syrian, Aramitess.
H762: Feminine of H761; (only adverbially) in Aramaean: - in the Syrian language (tongue), in Syriack.
H763: From H758 and the dual of H5104; Aram of (the) two rivers (Euphrates and Tigris) or Mesopotamia: - Aham-naharaim, Mesopotamia.
H764: From H759; palatial ; Armoni, an Israelite: - Armoni.
H765: From H7442; stridulous ; Aran, an Edomite: - Aran.
H766: From the same as H765 (in the sense of strength); the ash tree (from its toughness): - ash.
H767: The same as H766; Oren, an Israelite: - Oren.
H768: Of uncertain derivation; the hare: - hare.
H769: From H7442; a brawling stream; the Arnon, a river east of the Jordan; also its territory: - Arnon.
H770: Probably from the same as H769; noisy ; Arnan, an Israelite: - Arnan.

H1583: From H1580 and H410; reward of God ; Gamliel, an Israelite: - Gamaliel.

H1592: From H1589; theft ; Genubath, an Edomitish prince: - Genubath.
H1593: Feminine of H1588; a garden: - garden.
H1595: From an unused root meaning to store ; treasure ; by implication a coffer: - chest, treasury.

H1598: A primitive root; to hedge about, that is, (generally) protect: - defend.
H1599: From H1598; gardener ; Ginnethon or Ginnetho, an Israelite: - Ginnetho, Ginnethon.

H1612: From an unused root meaning to bend ; a vine (as twining), especially the grape: - vine, tree.

H2761: (Chaldee); a root probably allied to the equivalent of H2787; to scorch: - singe.
H2762: From H2760; properly a net, that is, (by analogy) lattice: - lattice.
H2763: A primitive root; to seclude ; specifically (by a ban) to devote to religious uses (especially destruction); physically and reflexively to be blunt as to the nose: - make accursed, consecrate, (utterly) destroy, devote, forfeit, have a flat nose, utterly (slay, make away).
H2764: From H2763; physically (as shutting in) a net (either literally or figuratively); usually a doomed object; abstractly extermination: - (ac-)curse (-d, -d thing), dedicated thing, things which should have been utterly destroyed, (appointed to) utter destruction, devoted (thing), net.
H2765: From H2763; devoted ; Chorem, a place in Palestine: - Horem.
H2766: From H2763; snubnosed ; Charim, an Israelite: - Harim.
H2767: From H2763; devoted ; Chormah, a place in Palestine: - Hormah.
H2768: From H2763; abrupt ; Chermon, a mount of Palestine: - Hermon.
H2769: Plural of H2768; Hermons, that is, its peaks: - the Hermonites.
H2770: From H2763; a sickle (as cutting): - sickle.
H2771: From H2787; parched ; Charan, the name of a man and also of a place: - Haran.
H2772: Patrial from H2773; a Choronite or inhabitant of Choronaim: - Horonite.
H2773: Dual of a derivative from H2356; double cave town ; Choronajim, a place in Moab: - Horonaim.
H2774: Of uncertain derivation; Charnepher, an Israelite: - Harnepher.
H2775: From an unused root meaning to scrape ; the itch ; also (perhaps from the mediating idea of H2777) the sun: - itch, sun.
H2776: The same as H2775; shining ; Cheres, a mount in Palestine: - Heres.
H2777: From H2775 (Apparently in the sense of a red tile used for scraping); a potsherd, that is, (by implication) a pottery ; the name of a gate at Jerusalem: - east.
H2778: A primitive root; to pull off, that is, (by implication) to expose (as by stripping); specifically to betroth (as if a surrender); figuratively to carp at, that is, defame ; denominatively (from H2779) to spend the winter: - betroth, blaspheme, defy, jeopard, rail, reproach, upbraid.
H2779: From H2778; properly the crop gathered, that is, (by implication) the autumn (and winter) season; figuratively ripeness of age: - cold, winter ([-house]), youth.
H2780: From H2778; reproachful ; an Israelite: - Hareph.
H2781: From H2778; contumely, disgrace, the pudenda: - rebuke, reproach (-fully), shame.
H2782: A prim root; properly to point sharply, that is, (literally) to wound ; figuratively to be alert, to decide: - bestir self, decide, decree, determine, maim, move.
H2783: (Chaldee) from a root corresponding to H2782 in the sense of vigor ; the loin (as the seat of strength): - loin.
H2784: Of uncertain derivation; a fetter ; figuratively a pain: - band.
H2785: From H2782; a sour grape (as sharp in taste): - kernel.
H2786: A primitive root; to grate the teeth: - gnash.
H2787: A primitive root; to glow, that is, literally (to melt, burn, dry up) or figuratively (to show or incite passion): - be angry, burn, dry, kindle.
H2789: A collateral form mediating between H2775 and H2791; a piece of pottery: - earth (-en), (pot-) sherd, + stone.
H2790: A primitive root; to scratch, that is, (by implication) to engrave, plough ; hence (from the use of tools) to fabricate (of any material); figuratively to devise (in a bad sense); hence (from the idea of secrecy) to be silent, to let alone ; hence (by implication) to be deaf (as an accompaniment of dumbness): - X altogether, cease, conceal, be deaf, devise, ear, graven, imagine, leave off speaking, hold peace, plow (-er, -man), be quiet, rest, practise secretly, keep silence, be silent, speak not a word, be still, hold tongue, worker.
H2791: From H2790; magical craft ; also silence: - cunning, secretly.
H2792: The same as H2791; Cheresh, a Levite: - Cheresh, a Levite: - Heresh.
H2793: From H2790; a forest (perhaps as furnishing the material for fabric): - bough, forest, shroud, wood.
H2794: Active participle of H2790; a fabricator or mechanic: - artificer.
H2795: From H2790; deaf (whether literal or spiritual): - deaf.
H2796: From H2790; a fabricator of any material: - artificer, (+) carpenter, craftsman, engraver, maker, + mason, skilful, (+) smith, worker, workman, such as wrought.
H2797: From H2792; magician ; Charsha, one of the Nethinim: - Harsha.
H2798: Plural of H2796; mechanics, the name of a valley in Jerusalem: - Charashim, craftsmen.
H2799: From H2790; mechanical work: - carving, cutting.
H2800: The same as H2799; Charosheth, a place in Palestine: - Harosheth.
H2801: A primitive root; to engrave: - graven.
H2802: From H2801 (but equivalent to H2793); forest ; Chereth, a thicket in Palestine: - Hereth.
H2803: A primitive root; properly to plait or interpenetrate, that is, (literally) to weave or (generally) to fabricate ; figuratively to plot or contrive (usually in a malicious sense); hence (from the mental effort) to think, regard, value, compute: - (make) account (of), conceive, consider, count, cunning (man, work, workman), devise, esteem, find out, forecast, hold, imagine, impute, invent, be like, mean, purpose, reckon (-ing be made), regard, think.
H2804: (Chaldee); corresponding to H2803; to regard: - repute.
H2805: From H2803; a belt or strap (as being interlaced): - curious girdle.
H2806: From H2803 and H1777; considerate judge ; Chasbaddanah, an Israelite: - Hasbadana.
H2807: From H2803; estimation ; Chashubah, an Israelite: - Hashubah.
H2808: From H2803; properly contrivance ; by implication intelligence: - account, device, reason.
H2809: The same as H2808; Cheshbon, a place East of the Jordan: - Heshbon.
H2810: From H2803; a contrivance, that is, actual (a warlike machine) or mental (a machination): - engine, invention.
H2811: From H2803 and H3050; Jah has regarded ; Chashabjah, the name of nine Israelites: - Hashabiah.
H2812: Feminine of H2808; inventiveness ; Chashnah, an Israelite: - Hashabnah.
H2813: From H2808 and H3050; thought of Jah ; Chashabnejah, the name of two Israelites: - Hashabniah.
H2814: A primitive root; to hush or keep quiet: - hold peace, keep silence, be silent, (be) still.
H2815: From H2803; intelligent ; Chashshub, the name of two or three Israelites: - Hashub, Hasshub.
H2816: (Chaldee) from a root corresponding to H2821; the dark: - darkness.
H2817: From H2834; nakedness ; Chasupha, one of the Nethinim: - Hashupha, Hasupha.
H2818: (Chaldee); a collateral root to one corresponding to H2363 in the sense of readiness ; to be necessary (from the idea of convenience) or (transitively) to need: - careful, have need of.
H2819: From a root corresponding to H2818; necessity: - be needful.
H2820: A prim root; to restrain or (reflexively) refrain ; by implication to refuse, spare, preserve ; also (by interchange with H2821) to observe: - assuage, X darken, forbear, hinder, hold back, keep (back), punish, refrain, reserve, spare, withhold.
H2821: A primitive root; to be dark (as withholding light); transitively to darken: - be black, be (make) dark, darken, cause darkness, be dim, hide.
H2822: From H2821; the dark ; hence (literally) darkness ; figuratively misery, destruction, death, ignorance, sorrow, wickedness: - dark (-ness), night, obscurity.
H2823: From H2821; dark (figuratively that is, obscure): - mean.
H2825: From H2821; darkness ; figuratively misery: - darkness.
H2826: A primitive root; to make (intransitively be) unsteady, that is, weak: - feeble.
H2827: (Chaldee) a root corresponding to H2826; to weaken, that is, crush: - subdue.
H2828: From the same as H2831; enriched ; Chashum, the name of two or three Israelites: - Hashum.
H2829: The same as H2831; opulent ; Cheshmon, a place in Palestine: - Heshmon.
H2830: Of uncertain derivation; probably bronze or polished spectrum metal: - amber.
H2831: From an unused root (probably meaning firm or capacious in resources); apparently wealthy: - princes.
H2832: Feminine of H2831; fertile ; Chasmonah, a place in the Desert: - Hashmonah.
H2833: From an unused root probably meaning to contain or sparkle ; perhaps a pocket (as holding the Urim and Thummim), or rich (as containing gems), used only of the gorget of the highpriest: - breastplate.
H2834: A primitive root; to strip off, that is, generally to make naked (for exertion or in disgrace), to drain away or bail up (a liquid): - make bare, clean, discover, draw out, take, uncover.
H2835: From H2834; properly drawn off, that is, separated; hence a small company (as divided from the rest): - little flock.
H2836: A primitive root; to cling, that is, join (figuratively) to love, delight in; elliptically (or by interchange for H2820) to deliver: - have a delight, (have a) desire, fillet, long, set (in) love.
H2838: Passive participle of H2836; attached, that is, a fence rail or rod connecting the posts or pillars: - fillet.
H2839: From H2836; conjoined, that is, a wheel spoke or rod connecting the hub with the rim: - felloe.
H2840: From an unused root meaning to bind together; combined, that is, the nave or hub of a wheel (as holding the spokes together): - spoke.
H2841: From the same as H2840; properly a combination or gathering, that is, of watery clouds: - dark.
H2842: By variation for H7179; dry grass: - chaff.
H2843: Patronymic from H2364; a Chushathite or descendant of Chushah: - Hushathite.
H2844: From H2865; concretely crushed ; also afraid ; abstractly terror: - broken, dismayed, dread, fear.
H2845: From H2865; terror ; Cheth, an aboriginal Canaanite: - Heth.
H2846: A primitive root; to lay hold of; especially to pick up fire: - heap, take (away).
H2848: From H2853; swathed, that is, a bandage: - roller.
H2850: Patronymic from H2845; a Chittite, or descendant of Cheth: - Hittite, Hittites.
H2852: A primitive root; properly to cut off, that is, (figuratively) to decree: - determine.
H2853: A primitive root; to swathe: - X at all, swaddle.
H2854: From H2853; a swathing cloth (figuratively): - swaddling band.
H2855: From H2853; enswathed ; Chethlon, a place in Palestine: - Hethlon.
H2856: A primitive root; to close up; especially to seal: - make an end, mark, seal (up), stop.
H2857: (Chaldee); a root corresponding to H2856; to seal: - seal.
H2858: Feminine active participle of H2856; a seal: - signet.
H2859: A primitive root; to give (a daughter) away in marriage; hence (generally) to contract affinity by marriage: - join in affinity, father in law, make marriages, mother in law, son in law.
H2860: From H2859; a relative by marriage (especially through the bride); figuratively a circumcised child (as a species of religious espousal): - bridegroom, husband, son in law.
H2862: A primitive root; to clutch: - take away.
H2863: From H2862; properly rapine ; figuratively robbery: - prey.
H2864: A primitive root; to force a passage, as by burglary; figuratively with oars: - dig (through), row.
H2865: A primitive root; properly to prostrate ; hence to break down, either (literally) by violence, or (figuratively) by confusion and fear: - abolish, affright, be (make) afraid, amaze, beat down, discourage, (cause to) dismay, go down, scare, terrify.
H2867: The same as H2866; Chathath, an Israelite: - Hathath.
H2868: (Chaldee); a primitive root; to rejoice: - be glad.
H2869: (Chaldee); from H2868; the same as H2896; good: - fine, good.
H2870: From H2895 and H410; pleasing (to) God ; Tabeel, the name of a Syrian and of a Persian: - Tabeal, Tabeel.
H2871: Passive participle of H2881; properly dyed, that is, a turban (probably as of colored stuff): - dyed attire.
H2872: From an unused root meaning to pile up; properly accumulated ; that is, (by implication) a summit: - middle, midst.
H2873: A primitive root; to slaughter (animals or men): - kill, (make) slaughter, slay.
H2874: From H2873; properly something slaughtered ; hence a beast (or meat, as butchered); abstractly butchery (or concretely a place of slaughter): - X beast, slaughter, X slay, X sore.
H2875: The same as H2874; massacre ; Tebach, the name of a Mesopotamian and of an Israelite: - Tebah.
H2876: From H2873; properly a butcher ; hence a lifeguardsman (because acting as executioner); also a cook (as usually slaughtering the animal for food): - cook, guard.
H2877: (Chaldee); the same as H2876; a lifeguardsman: - guard.
H2878: Feminine of H2874 and meaning the same: - flesh, slaughter.
H2879: Feminine of H2876; a female cook: - cook.
H2880: From H2878; slaughter ; Tibchath, a place in Syria: - Tibhath.
H2881: A primitive root; to dip: - dip, plunge.
H2882: From H2881 and H3050; Jah has dipped ; Tebaljah, an Israelite: - Tebaliah.
H2883: A primitive root; to sink: - drown, fasten, settle, sink.
H2884: Plural of H2885; rings ; Tabbaoth, one of the Nethinim: - Tabbaoth.
H2885: From H2883; properly a seal (as sunk into the wax), that is, signet (for sealing); hence (generically) a ring of any kind: - ring.
H2886: From H2895 and H7417; pleasing (to) Rimmon ; Tabrimmon, a Syrian: - Tabrimmon.
H2887: Probably of foreign derivation; Tebeth, the tenth Hebrew month: - Tebeth.
H2888: Of uncertain derivation; Tabbath, a place East of the Jordan: - Tabbath.
H2889: From H2891; pure (in a physical, chemical, ceremonial or moral sense): - clean, fair, pure (-ness).
H2891: A primitive root; properly to be bright ; that is, (by implication) to be pure (physically sound, clear, unadulterated ; Levitically uncontaminated ; morally innocent or holy): - be (make, make self, pronounce) clean, cleanse (self), purge, purify (-ier, self).
H2892: From H2891; literally brightness ; ceremonially purification: - clearness, glory, purifying.
H2893: Feminine of H2892; ceremonial purification ; moral purity: - X is cleansed, cleansing, purification (-fying).
H2894: A primitive root; to sweep away: - sweep.
H2895: A primitive root, to be (transitively do or make) good (or well) in the widest sense: - be (do) better, cheer, be (do, seem) good, (make), goodly, X please, (be, do, go, play) well.
H2896: From H2895; good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well): - beautiful, best, better, bountiful, cheerful, at ease, X fair (word), (be in) favour, fine, glad, good (deed, -lier, liest, -ly, -ness, -s), graciously, joyful, kindly, kindness, liketh (best), loving, merry, X most, pleasant, + pleaseth, pleasure, precious, prosperity, ready, sweet, wealth, welfare, (be) well ([-favoured]).
H2897: The same as H2896; good ; Tob, a region apparently East of the Jordan: - Tob.
H2898: From H2895; good (as a noun), in the widest sense, especially goodness (superlatively concrete, the best), beauty, gladness, welfare: - fair, gladness, good (-ness, thing, -s), joy, go well with.
H2899: From H2896 and H138; pleasing (to) Adonijah ; Tob-Adonijah, an Israelite: - Tob-adonijah.
H2900: From H2896 and H3050; goodness of Jehovah ; Tobijah, the name of three Israelites and of one Samaritan: - Tobiah, Tobijah.
H2901: A primitive root; to spin: - spin.
H2902: A primitive root; to smear, especially with lime: - daub, overlay, plaister, smut.
H2903: From an unused root meaning to go around or bind ; a fillet for the forehead: - frontlet.
H2904: A primitive root; to pitch over or reel ; hence (transitively) to cast down or out: - carry away, (utterly) cast (down, forth, out), send out.
H2905: From an unused root meaning to range in a regular manner; a row ; hence a wall: - row.
H2906: (Chaldee); corresponding to H6697; a rock or hill: - mountain.
H2907: A primitive root; to pounce as a bird of prey: - haste.
H2908: (Chaldee); from a root corresponding to H2901; hunger (as twisting): - fasting.
H2909: A primitive root; to stretch a bow, as an archer: - [bow-] shot.
H2910: From H2909 (or H2902) in the sense of overlaying ; (in the plural only) the kidneys (as being covered); hence (figuratively) the inmost thought: - inward parts.
H2911: From H2912; a hand mill ; hence a millstone: - to grind.
H2912: A primitive root; to grind meal; hence to be a concubine (that being their employment): - grind (-er).
H2913: From H2912; a hand mill ; hence (figuratively) chewing: - grinding.
H2914: From an unused root meaning to burn ; a boil or ulcer (from the inflammation), especially a tumor in the anus or pudenda (the piles): - emerod.
H2915: From (the equivalent of) H2902; mortar or plaster: - daubing.
H2916: From an unused root meaning apparently to be sticky (rather perhaps a denominative from H2894, through the idea of dirt to be swept away); mud or clay ; figuratively calamity: - clay, dirt, mire.
H2917: (Chaldee); perhaps by interchange for a word corresponding to H2916; clay: - miry.
H2918: Feminine of (an equivalent to) H2905; a wall ; hence a fortress or a hamlet: - (goodly) castle, habitation, palace, row.
H2919: From H2926; dew (as covering vegetation): - dew.
H2921: A primitive root; properly to cover with pieces; that is, (by implication) to spot or variegate (as tapestry): - clouted, with divers colours, spotted.
H2922: Apparently from H2921 in the (original) sense of covering (for protection); a lamb (compare H2924): - lamb.
H2923: From the plural of H2922; lambs ; Telaim, a place in Palestine: - Telaim.
H2924: By variation for H2922; a lamb: - lamb.
H2925: From H2904; overthrow or rejection: - captivity.
H2926: A primitive root; properly to strew over, that is, (by implication) to cover in or plate (with beams): - cover.
H2927: (Chaldee); corresponding to H2926; to cover with shade: - have a shadow.
H2928: From an unused root meaning to break up or treat violently; oppression ; Telem, the name of a place in Idumaea, also of a temple doorkeeper: - Telem.
H2929: From the same as H2728; oppressive ; Talmon, a temple doorkeeper: - Talmon.
H2930: A primitive root; to be foul, especially in a ceremonial or moral sense (contaminated): - defile (self), pollute (self), be (make, make self, pronounce) unclean, X utterly.
H2931: From H2930; foul in a religious sense: - defiled, + infamous, polluted (-tion), unclean.
H2932: From H2930; religious impurity: - filthiness, unclean (-ness).
H2933: A collateral form of H2930; to be impure in a religious sense: - be defiled, be reputed vile.
H2934: A primitive root; to hide (by covering over): - hide, lay privily, in secret.
H2935: From an unused root probably meaning to weave ; a basket (of interlaced osiers): - basket.
H2936: A primitive root; to soil: - defile.
H2937: A primitive root; to wander ; causatively to lead astray: - seduce.
H2938: A primitive root; to taste ; figuratively to perceive: - X but, perceive, taste.
H2939: (Chaldee); corresponding to H2938; to taste ; causatively to feed: - make to eat, feed.
H2940: From H2938; properly a taste, that is, (figuratively) perception ; by implication intelligence ; transitively a mandate: - advice, behaviour, decree, discretion, judgment, reason, taste, understanding.
H2941: (Chaldee); from H2939; properly a taste, that is, (as in H2940) a judicial sentence: - account, X to be commanded, commandment, matter.
H2942: (Chaldee); from H2939, and equivalent to H2941; properly flavor ; figuratively judgment (both subjectively and objectively); hence account (both subjectively and objectively): - + chancellor, + command, commandment, decree, + regard, taste, wisdom.
H2943: A primitive root; to load a beast: - lade.
H2944: A primitive root; to stab: - thrust through.
H2945: From H2952 (perhaps referring to the tripping gait of children); a family (mostly used collectively in the singular): - (little) children (ones), families.
H2946: A primitive root; to flatten out or extend (as a tent); figuratively to nurse a child (as promotive of growth); or perhaps a denominative from H2947, from dandling on the palms: - span, swaddle.
H2947: From H2946; a spread of the hand, that is, a palm breadth (not " span" of the fingers); architecturally a corbel (as a supporting palm): - coping, hand-breadth.
H2948: From H2946 (the same as H2947): - hand-breadth (broad).
H2950: A primitive root; properly to stick on as a patch; figuratively to impute falsely: - forge (-r), sew up.
H2951: Of foreign derivation; a military governor: - captain.
H2952: A primitive root; apparently to trip (with short steps) coquettishly: - mince.
H2953: (Chaldee); from a root corresponding to H6852, and meaning the same as H6856; a finger nail ; also a hoof or claw: - nail.
H2954: A primitive root; properly apparently to be thick ; figuratively to be stupid: - be fat.
H2955: Probably from H5197; a dropping (of ointment); Taphath, an Israelitess: - Taphath.
H2956: A primitive root; to drive on; figuratively to follow close: - continual.
H2957: (Chaldee); corresponding to H2956; to expel: - drive.
H2958: A variation of H2962; not yet: - before.
H2959: A primitive root; to overburden: - weary.
H2960: From H2959; a burden: - cumbrance, trouble.
H2961: From an unused root apparently meaning to be moist ; properly dripping ; hence fresh (that is, recently made such): - new, putrefying.
H2962: From an unused root apparently meaning to interrupt or suspend ; properly non-occurrence ; used adverbially not yet or before: - before, ere, not yet.
H2963: A primitive root; to pluck off or pull to pieces; causatively to supply with food (as in morsels): - catch, X without doubt, feed, ravin, rend in pieces, X surely, tear (in pieces).
H2964: From H2963; something torn, that is, a fragment, for example a fresh leaf, prey, food: - leaf, meat, prey, spoil.
H2965: From H2963; recently torn off, that is, fresh: - pluckt off.
H2966: Feminine (collectively) of H2964; prey, that is, flocks devoured by animals: - ravin, (that which was) torn (of beasts, in pieces).
H2967: (Chaldee); from a name of foreign derivation; a Tarpelite (collectively) or inhabitant of Tarpel, a place in Assyria: - Tarpelites.
H2968: A primitive root; to desire: - long.
H2969: A primitive root; to be suitable: - appertain.
H2970: From H238 and H3050; heard of Jah ; Jaazanjah, the name of four Israelites: - Jaazaniah. Compare H3153.
H2971: From H215; enlightener ; Jair, the name of four Israelites: - Jair.
H2972: Patronymic from H2971; a Jairite or descendant of Jair: - Jairite.
H2973: A primitive root; properly to be slack, that is, (figuratively) to be foolish: - dote, be (become, do) foolish (-ly).
H2974: A primitive root (probably rather the same as H2973 through the idea of mental weakness); properly to yield, especially assent ; hence (positively) to undertake as an act of volition: - assay, begin, be content, please, take upon, X willingly, would.
H2975: Of Egyptian origin; a channel, for example a fosse, canal, shaft; specifically the Nile, as the one river of Egypt, including its collateral trenches; also the Tigris, as the main river of Assyria: - brook, flood, river, stream.
H2976: A primitive root; to desist, that is, (figuratively) to despond: - (cause to) despair, one that is desperate, be no hope.
H2977: From the same root as H803 and H3050; founded of Jah ; Joshijah, the name of two Israelites: - Josiah.
H2979: From the same as H871; stepping ; Jeatherai, an Israelite: - Jeaterai.
H2980: A primitive root; to bawl: - cry out.
H2981: From H2986; produce, that is, a crop or (figuratively) wealth: - fruit, increase.
H2982: From H947; trodden, that is, threshing place; Jebus, the aboriginal name of Jerusalem: - Jebus.
H2983: Patrial from H2982; a Jebusite or inhabitant of Jebus: - Jebusite(-s).
H2984: From H977; choice ; Jibchar, an Israelite: - Ibhar.
H2985: From H995; intelligent ; Jabin, the name of two Canaanitish kings: - Jabin.
H2986: A primitive root; properly to flow ; causatively to bring (especially with pomp): - bring (forth), carry, lead (forth).
H2987: (Chaldee); corresponding to H2986; to bring: - bring, carry.
H2988: From H2986; a stream: - [water-] course, stream.
H2989: The same as H2988; Jabal, an antediluvian: - Jabal.
H2990: From H2986; having running sores: - wen.
H2991: From H1104 and H5971; devouring people ; Jibleam, a place in Palestine: - Ibleam.
H2992: A primitive root of doubtful meaning; used only as a denominative from H2993; to marry a (deceased) brother's widow: - perform the duty of a husband's brother, marry.
H2993: From (the original of) H2992; a brother-in-law: - husband'sbrother.
H2994: Feminine participle of H2992; a sister-in-law: - brother's wife, sister in law.
H2995: From H1129 and H410; built of God ; Jabneel, the name of two places in Palestine: - Jabneel.
H2996: From H1129; a building ; Jabneh, a place in Palestine: - Jabneh.
H2997: From H1129 and H3050; built of Jah ; Jibnejah, an Israelite: - Ibneiah.
H2998: From H1129 and H3050; building of Jah ; Jibnijah, an Israelite: - Ibnijah.
H2999: Probably from H1238; pouring forth; Jabbok, a river East of the Jordan: - Jabbok.
H3000: From H1288 and H3050; blessed of Jah ; Jeberekjah, an Israelite: - Jeberechiah.
