H3428: From H3427 and H1; seat of (his) father ; Jeshebab, an Israelite: - Jeshebeab.
H3429: From the active participle of H3427 and H7674, with a preposition and the article interposed; sitting in the seat ; Josheb-bash-Shebeht, an Israelite: - that sat in the seat.
H3430: From H3427 and H5011, with a pronominal suffix and a preposition interposed; his dwelling (is) in Nob ; Jishbo-be-Nob, a Philistine: - Ishbi-benob [from the margin].
H3431: From H7623; he will praise ; Jishbach, an Israelite: - Ishbah.
H3432: Patronymic from H3437; a Jashubite, or descendant of Jashub: - Jashubites.
H3433: Shown as the first form; from H7725 and H3899; returner of bread ; Jashubi-Lechem, an Israelite; but probably the text should be pointed (as in the second form) and rendered (they were) inhabitants of Lechem, that is, of Bethlehem (by contraction): - Jashubi-lehem. [Probably the text should be pointed Yoshebey Lechem, yo-sheh-bay leh-khem, and rendered " (they were) inhabitants of Lechem," That is,of Bethlehem (by contraction). Compare H3902.]
H3434: From H7725 and H5971; people will return ; Jashobam, the name of two or three Israelites: - Jashobeam.
H3435: From an unused root corresponding to H7662; he will leave ; Jishbak, a son of Abraham: - Ishbak.
H3436: From H3427 and H7186; a hard seat ; Joshbekashah, an Israelite: - Joshbekashah.
H3437: From H7725; he will return ; Jashub, the name of two Israelites: - Jashub.
H3438: From H7737; he will level ; Jishvah, an Israelite: - Ishvah, Isvah.
H3439: From the same as H3445 and H3050; Jah will empty ; Jeshochajah, an Israelite: - Jeshoaiah.
H3440: From H7737; level ; Jishvi, the name of two Israelites: - Ishuai, Ishvi, Isui, Jesui.
H3441: Patronymic from H3440; a Jishvite (collectively) or descendant of Jishvi: - Jesuites.
H3442: For H3091; he will save ; Jeshua, the name of two Israelites, also of a place in Palestine: - Jeshua.
H3444: Feminine passive participle of H3467; something saved, that is, (abstractly) deliverance ; hence aid, victory, prosperity: - deliverance, health, help (-ing), salvation, save, saving (health), welfare.
H3445: From an unused root meaning to gape (as the empty stomach); hunger: - casting down.
H3446: From H7831; he will laugh ; Jischak, the heir of Abraham: - Isaac. Compare H3327.
H3447: A primitive root; to extend: - hold out.
H3448: From the same as H3426; extant ; Jishai, David's father: - Jesse.
H3449: From H5383 and H3050; Jah will lend ; Jishshijah, the name of five Israelites: - Ishiah, Isshiah, Ishijah, Jesiah.
H3450: From H7760 and H410; God will place ; Jesimael, an Israelite: - Jesimiel.
H3451: From H3456; desolation: - let death seize [from the margin].
H3452: From H3456; a desolation: - desert, Jeshimon, solitary, wilderness.
H3453: From H3486; an old man: - (very) aged (man), ancient, very old.
H3454: From H3453; aged ; Jeshishai, an Israelite: - Jeshishai.
H3455: A primitive root; to place ; intransitively to be placed: - be put (set).
H3456: A primitive root; to lie waste: - be desolate.
H3457: From H3456; desolate ; Jishma, an Israelite: - Ishma.
H3458: From H8085 and H410; God will hear ; Jishmael, the name of Abraham's oldest son, and of five Israelites: - Ishmael.
H3459: Patronymic from H3458; a Jishmaelite or descendant of Jishmael: - Ishmaelite.
H3460: From H8085 and H3050; Jah will hear ; Jishmajah, the name of two Israelites: - Ishmaiah.
H3461: From H8104; preservative ; Jishmerai, an Israelite: - Ishmerai.
H3462: A primitive root; properly to be slack or languid, that is, (by implication) sleep (figuratively to die); also to grow old, stale or inveterate: - old (store), remain long, (make to) sleep.
H3463: From H3462; sleepy: - asleep, (one out of) sleep (-eth, -ing), slept.
H3464: The same as H3463; Jashen, an Israelite: - Jashen.
H3466: Feminine of H3465; Jeshanah, a place in Palestine: - Jeshanah.
H3467: A primitive root; properly to be open, wide or free, that is, (by implication) to be safe ; causatively to free or succor: - X at all, avenging, defend, deliver (-er), help, preserve, rescue, be safe, bring (having) salvation, save (-iour), get victory.
H3468: From H3467; liberty, deliverance, prosperity: - safety, salvation, saving.
H3469: From H3467; saving ; Jishi, the name of four Israelites: - Ishi.
H3470: From H3467 and H3050; Jah has saved ; Jeshajah, the name of seven Israelites: - Isaiah, Jesaiah, Jeshaiah.
H3471: From an unused root meaning to polish ; a gem supposed to be jasper (from the resemblance in name): - jasper.
H3472: Perhaps from H8192; he will scratch ; Jishpah, an Israelite: - Ispah.
H3473: Probably from the same as H8227; he will hide ; Jishpan, an Israelite: - Ishpan.
H3474: A primitive root; to be straight or even ; figuratively to be (causatively to make) right, pleasant, prosperous: - direct, fit, seem good (meet), + please (well), be (esteem, go) right (on), bring (look, make, take the) straight (way), be upright (-ly).
H3475: From H3474; the right ; Jesher, an Israelite: - Jesher.
H3476: From H3474; the right: - equity, meet, right, upright (-ness).
H3477: From H3474; straight (literally or figuratively): - convenient, equity, Jasher, just, meet (-est), + pleased well right (-eous), straight, (most) upright (-ly, -ness).
H3478: From H8280 and H410; he will rule as God ; Jisrael, a symbolical name of Jacob; also (typically) of his posterity: - Israel.
H3480: By variation from H3477 and H410 with directive enclitic; right towards God ; Jesarelah, an Israelite: - Jesharelah. Compare H841
H3481: Patronymic from H3478; a Jisreelite or descendant of Jisrael: - of Israel, Israelite.
H3482: Feminine of H3481; a Jisreelitess or female descendant of Jisrael: - Israelitish.
H3484: From H3474; upright ; Jeshurun, a symbolical name for Israel: - Jeshurun.
H3485: From H5375 and H7939; he will bring a reward ; Jissaskar, a son of Jacob: - Issachar.
H3486: From an unused root meaning to blanch ; gray haired, that is, an aged man: - stoop for age.
H3487: (Chaldee); corresponding to H853; a sign of the object of a verb: - + whom.
H3488: (Chaldee); corresponding to H3427; to sit or dwell: - dwell, (be) set, sit.
H3489: From an unused root meaning to pin through or fast; a peg: - nail, paddle, pin, stake.
H3490: From an unused root meaning to be lonely ; a bereaved person: - fatherless (child), orphan.
H3491: Passive participle of H3498; properly what is left, that is, (by implication) a gleaning: - range.
H3492: From H3498; redundant ; Jattir, a place in Palestine: - Jattir.
H3493: (Chaldee); corresponding to H3492; preeminent ; adverbially very: - exceeding (-ly), excellent.
H3494: Probably from H8518; it will hang, that is, high; Jithlah, a place in Palestine: - Jethlah.
H3495: From the same as H3490; orphanage ; Jithmah, an Israelite: - Ithmah.
H3496: From an unused root meaning to endure, and H410; continued of God ; Jathniel, an Israelite: - Jathniel.
H3497: From the same as H8577; extensive ; Jithnan, a place in Palestine: - Ithnan.
H3498: A primitive root; to jut over or exceed ; by implication to excel ; (intransitively) to remain or be left ; causatively to leave, cause to abound, preserve: - excel, leave (a remnant), left behind, too much, make plenteous, preserve, (be, let) remain (-der, -ing, -nant), reserve, residue, rest.
H3499: Properly an overhanging, that is, (by implication) an excess, superiority, remainder ; also a small rope (as hanging free): - + abundant, cord, exceeding, excellency (-ent), what they leave, that hath left, plentifully, remnant, residue, rest, string, with.
H3500: The same as H3499 Jether, the name of five or six Israelites and of one Midianite: - Jether, Jethro. Compare H3503.
H3501: By variation for H3502; Jithra, an Israelite (or Ishmaelite): - Ithra.
H3502: Feminine of H3499; properly excellence, that is, (by implication) wealth: - abundance, riches.
H3503: From H3499 with pronominal suffix; his excellence ; Jethro, Moses' father in law: - Jethro. Compare H3500.
H3504: From H3498; preeminence, gain: - better, excellency (-leth), profit (-able).
H3505: Patronymic from H3500; a Jithrite or descendant of Jether: - Ithrite.
H3506: From H3498; excellent ; Jithran, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite: - Ithran.
H3507: From H3499 and H5971; excellence of people ; Jithream, a son of David: - Ithream.
H3508: Feminine active participle of H3498; the lobe or flap of the liver (as if redundant or outhanging): - caul.
H3509: Of uncertain derivation; Jetheth, an Edomite: - Jetheth.
H3510: A primitive root; properly to feel pain ; by implication to grieve ; figuratively to spoil: - grieving, mar, have pain, make sad (sore), (be) sorrowful.
H3511: From H3510; suffering (physical or mental), adversity: - grief, pain, sorrow.
H3512: A primitive root; to despond ; causatively to deject: - broken, be grieved, make sad.
H3513: A primitive root; to be heavy, that is, in a bad sense (burdensome, severe, dull) or in a good sense (numerous, rich, honorable); causatively to make weighty (in the same two senses): - abounding with, more grievously afflict, boast, be chargeable, X be dim, glorify, be (make) glorious (things), glory, (very) great, be grievous, harden, be (make) heavy, be heavier, lay heavily, (bring to, come to, do, get, be had in) honour (self), (be) honourable (man), lade, X more be laid, make self many, nobles, prevail, promote (to honour), be rich, be (go) sore, stop.
H3514: From H3513; weight, multitude, vehemence: - grievousness, heavy, great number.
H3515: From H3513; heavy ; figuratively in a good sense (numerous) or in a bad sense (severe, difficult, stupid): - (so) great, grievous, hard (-ened), (too) heavy (-ier), laden, much, slow, sore, thick.
H3516: The same as H3515; the liver (as the heaviest of the viscera): - liver.
H3517: Feminine of H3515; difficulty: - X heavily.
H3518: A primitive root; to expire or (causatively) to extinguish (fire, light, anger): - go (put) out, quench.
H3519: From H3513; properly weight ; but only figuratively in a good sense, splendor or copiousness: - glorious (-ly), glory, honour (-able).
H3520: Irregular feminine passive participle of H3513; weightiness ; that is, magnificence, wealth: - carriage, all glorious, stately.
H3521: From the same as H3525 in the sense of limitation ; sterile ; Cabul, the name of two places in Palestine: - Cabul.
H3522: From an unused root meaning to heap up; hilly ; Cabbon, a place in Palestine: - Cabbon.
H3523: From H3527 in the original sense of plaiting ; a matrass (of intertwined materials): - pillow.
H3524: From H3727; vast, whether in extent (figuratively of power, mighty ; of time, aged), or in number, many: - + feeble, mighty, most, much, strong, valiant.
H3525: From an unused root meaning to twine or braid together; a fetter: - fetter.
H3526: A primitive root; to trample ; hence to wash (properly by stamping with the feet), whether literally (including the fulling process) or figuratively: - fuller, wash (-ing).
H3527: A primitive root; properly to plait together, that is, (figuratively) to augment (especially in number or quantity, to accumulate): - in abundance, multiply.
H3528: From H3527; properly extent of time, that is, a great while ; hence long ago, formerly, hitherto: - already, (seeing that which), now.
H3529: The same as H3528; length ; Kebar, a river of Mesopotamia: - Chebar. Compare H2249.
H3530: Feminine of H3528; properly length, that is, a measure (of uncertain dimension): - X little.
H3531: From H3527 in its original sense; a sieve (as netted): - sieve.
H3532: From an unused root meaning to dominate ; a ram (just old enough to butt): - lamb, sheep.
H3533: A primitive root; to tread down; hence negatively to disregard ; positively to conquer, subjugate, violate: - bring into bondage, force, keep under, subdue, bring into subjection.
H3534: From H3533; a footstool (as trodden upon): - footstool.
H3535: Feminine of H3532; a ewe: - (ewe) lamb.
H3536: From H3533; a smelting furnace (as reducing metals): - furnace.
H3537: From an unused root meaning to deepen ; properly a pail ; but generally of earthenware; a jar for domestic purposes: - barrel, pitcher.
H3538: (Chaldee); from a root corresponding to H3576; false: - lying.
H3539: From the same as H3537 in the sense of striking fire from a metal forged; a sparkling gem, probably the ruby: - agate.
H3540: Of foreign origin; Kedorlaomer, an early Persian king: - Chedorlaomer.
H3541: From the prefix K and H1931; properly like this, that is, by implication (of manner) thus (or so); also (of place) here (or hither); or (of time) now: - also, here, + hitherto, like, on the other side, so (and much), such, on that manner, (on) this (manner, side, way, way and that way), + mean while, yonder.
H3543: A primitive root; to be weak, that is, (figuratively) to despond (causatively rebuke), or (of light, the eye) to grow dull: - darken, be dim, fail, faint, restrain, X utterly.
H3544: From H3543; feeble, obscure: - somewhat dark, darkish, wax dim, heaviness, smoking.
H3545: Feminine of H3544; properly a weakening ; figuratively alleviation, that is, cure: - healing.
H3546: (Chaldee); a root corresponding to H3201 and H3557; to be able: - be able, could.
H3547: A primitive root, apparently meaning to mediate in religious services; but used only as denominative from H3548; to officiate as a priest; figuratively to put on regalia: - deck, be (do the office of a, execute the, minister in the) priest ('s office).
H3548: Active participle of H3547; literally one officiating, a priest ; also (by courtesy) an acting priest (although a layman): - chief ruler, X own, priest, prince, principal officer.
H3550: From H3547; priesthood: - priesthood, priest's office.
H3551: (Chaldee); from a root corresponding to H3854 in the sense of piercing ; a window (as a perforation): - window.
H3552: Of foreign derivation; Kub, a country near Egypt: - Chub.
H3553: From an unused root meaning to be high or rounded ; a helmet (as arched): - helmet. Compare H6959.
H3554: A primitive root; properly to prick or penetrate ; hence to blister (as smarting or eating into): - burn.
H3556: Probably from the same as H3522 (in the sense of rolling) or H3554 (in the sense of blazing); a star (as round or as shining); figuratively a prince: - star ([-gazer]).
H3557: A primitive root; properly to keep in ; hence to measure ; figuratively to maintain (in various senses): - (be able to, can) abide, bear, comprehend, contain, feed, forbearing, guide, hold (-ing in), nourish (-er), be present, make provision, receive, sustain, provide sustenance (victuals).
H3558: From an unused root meaning to store away; a jewel (probably gold beads): - tablet.
H3559: A primitive root; properly to be erect (that is, stand perpendicular);. hence (causatively) to set up, in a great variety of applications, whether literal (establish, fix, prepare, apply), or figurative (appoint, render sure, proper or prosperous): - certain (-ty), confirm, direct, faithfulness, fashion, fasten, firm, be fitted, be fixed, frame, be meet, ordain, order, perfect, (make) preparation, prepare (self), provide, make provision, (be, make) ready, right, set (aright, fast, forth), be stable, (e-) stablish, stand, tarry, X very deed.
H3560: Probably from H3559; established ; Kun, a place in Syria: - Chun.
H3561: From H3559; something prepared, that is, a sacrificial wafer: - cake.
H3562: From H3559 and H3050; Jah has sustained ; Conanjah, the name of two Israelites: - Conaniah, Cononiah. Compare H3663.
H3563: From an unused root meaning to hold together; a cup (as a container), often figuratively a lot (as if a potion); also some unclean bird, probably an owl (perhaps from the cup like cavity of its eye): - cup, (small) owl. Compare H3599.
H3564: From an unused root meaning properly to dig through; a pot or furnace (as if excavated): - furnace. Compare H3600.
H3565: From H3564 and H6227; furnace of smoke ; Cor-Ashan, a place in Palestine: - Chor-ashan.
H3566: From the Persian; Koresh (or Cyrus), the Persian king: - Cyrus.
H3568: Probably of foreign origin; Cush (or Ethiopia), the name of a son of Ham, and of his territory; also of an Israelite: - Chush, Cush, Ethiopia.
H3569: Patronymic from H3568; a Cushite, or descendant of Cush: - Cushi, Cushite, Ethiopian (-s).
H3570: The same as H3569; Cushi, the name of two Israelites: - Cushi.
H3571: Feminine of H3569; a Cushite woman: - Ethiopian.
H3572: Perhaps from H3568; Cushan, a region of Arabia: - Cushan.
H3573: Apparently from H3572 and the dual of H7564; Cushan of double wickedness ; Cushan-Rishathajim, a Mesopotamian king: - Chushan-rishathayim.
H3574: From H3787; prosperity ; in plural freedom: - X chain.
H3575: Of foreign origin; Cuth or Cuthah, a province of Assyria: - Cuth.
H3576: A primitive root; to lie (that is, deceive), literally or figuratively: - fail, (be found a, make a) liar, lie, lying, be in vain.
H3577: From H3576; falsehood ; literally (untruth) or figuratively (idol): - deceitful, false, leasing, + liar, lie, lying.
H3578: From H3576; fallacious ; Cozeba, a place in Palestine: - Choseba.
H3579: From H3576; false ; Cozbi, a Midianitess: - Cozbi.
H3580: From H3576; falsified ; Kezib, a place in Palestine: - Chezib.
H3581: From an unused root meaning to be firm ; vigor, literally (force, in a good or a bad sense) or figuratively (capacity, means, produce); also (from its hardiness) a large lizard: - ability, able, chameleon, force, fruits, might, power (-ful), strength, substance, wealth.
H3582: A primitive root; to secrete, by act or word; hence (intensively) to destroy: - conceal, cut down (off), desolate, hide.
H3583: A primitive root; to paint (with stibium): - paint.
H3584: A primitive root; to be untrue, in word (to lie, feign, disown) or deed (to disappoint, fail, cringe): - deceive, deny, dissemble, fail, deal falsely, be found liars, (be-) lie, lying, submit selves.
H3585: From H3584; literally a failure of flesh, that is, emaciation ; figuratively hypocrisy: - leanness, lies, lying.
H3587: From H3554; a brand or scar: - burning.
H3588: A primitive particle (the full form of the prepositional prefix) indicating causal relations of all kinds, antecedent or consequent; (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjugation or adverb; often largely modified by other particles annexed: - and, + (forasmuch, inasmuch, where-) as, assured [-ly], + but, certainly, doubtless, + else, even, + except, for, how, (because, in, so, than) that, + nevertheless, now, rightly, seeing, since, surely, then, therefore, + (al-) though, + till, truly, + until, when, whether, while, who, yea, yet,
H3589: From a primitive root meaning to strike ; a crushing ; figuratively calamity: - destruction.
H3590: From the same as H3589 (compare H3539); properly something struck off, that is, a spark (as struck): - spark.
H3591: From the same as H3589; properly something to strike with, that is, a dart (perhaps smaller than H2595): - lance, shield, spear, target.
H3592: The same as H3591; Kidon, a place in Palestine: - Chidon.
H3593: Of uncertain derivation; perhaps tumult: - battle.
H3594: From H3559; properly a statue, that is, idol; but used (by euphemism) for some heathen deity (perhaps corresponding to Priapus or Baal-peor): - Chiun.
H3595: From the same as H3564; properly something round (as excavated or bored), that is, a chafing dish for coals or a caldron for cooking; hence (from similarity of form) a washbowl ; also (for the same reason) a pulpit or platform: - hearth, laver, pan, scaffold.
H3596: From H3557 in the sense of withholding ; niggardly: - churl.
H3597: From an unused root meaning to clap or strike with noise; a club or sledge hammer: - hammer.
H3598: From the same as H3558; a cluster of stars, that is, the Pleiades: - Pleiades, seven stars.
H3599: A form for H3563; a cup ; also a bag for money or weights: - bag, cup, purse.
H3600: A form for H3564 (only in the dual); a cooking range (consisting of two parallel stones, across which the boiler is set): - ranges for pots.
H3601: From H3787; literally a director, that is, the spindle or shank of a distaff (H6418) by which it is twirled: - spindle.
H3602: From H3541; just so, referring to the previous or following context: - after that (this) manner, this matter, (even) so, in such a case, thus.
H3603: From H3769; a circle, that is, (by implication) a circumjacent tract or region, especially the Ghor or valley of the Jordan; also a (round) loaf ; also a talent (or large (round) coin): - loaf, morsel, piece, plain, talent.
H3604: (Chaldee); corresponding to H3603; a talent: - talent.
H3605: From H3634; properly the whole ; hence all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense): - (in) all (manner, [ye]), altogether, any (manner), enough, every (one, place, thing), howsoever, as many as, [no-] thing, ought, whatsoever, (the) whole, whoso (-ever).
H3606: (Chaldee); corresponding to H3605: - all, any, + (forasmuch) as, + be- (for this) cause, every, + no (manner, -ne), + there (where) -fore, + though, what (where, who) -soever, (the) whole.
H3607: A primitive root; to restrict, by act (hold back or in) or word (prohibit): - finish, forbid, keep (back), refrain, restrain, retain, shut up, be stayed, withhold.
H3608: From H3607; a prison : - prison. Compare H3610, H3628.
H3609: Apparently from H3607 and H1; restraint of (his) father ; Kilab, an Israelite: - Chileab.
H3610: Dual of H3608 in the original sense of separation ; two heterogeneities: - divers seeds (-e kinds), mingled (seed).
H3611: From an unused root meaning to yelp, or else to attack ; a dog ; hence (by euphemism) a male prostitute: - dog.
H3612: Perhaps a form of H3611, or else from the same root in the sense of forcible ; Caleb, the name of three Israelites: - Caleb.
H3613: From H3612 and H672; Caleb-Ephrathah, a place in Egypt (if the text is correct): - Caleb-ephrathah.
H3614: The first form is probably by erroneous transcription for the second form; patronymic from H3612; a Calebite or descendant of Caleb: - of the house of Caleb.
H3615: A primitive root; to end, whether intransitively (to cease, be finished, perish) or transitively (to complete, prepare, consume): - accomplish, cease, consume (away), determine, destroy (utterly), be (when. .. were) done, (be an) end (of), expire, (cause to) fail, faint, finish, fulfil, X fully, X have, leave (off), long, bring to pass, wholly reap, make clean riddance, spend, quite take away, waste.
H3617: From H3615; a completion ; adverbially completely ; also destruction: - altogether, (be, utterly) consume (-d), consummation (-ption), was determined, (full, utter) end, riddance.
H3618: From H3634; a bride (as if perfect); hence a son's wife: - bride, daughter-in-law, spouse.
H3619: From the same as H3611; a bird trap (as furnished with a clapstick or treadle to spring it); hence a basket (as resembling a wicker cage): - basket, cage.
H3620: The same as H3619; Kelub, the name of two Israelites: - Chelub.
H3621: A form of H3612; Kelubai, an Israelite: - Chelubai.
H3622: From H3615; completed ; Keluhai, an Israelite: - Chelluh.
H3623: Denominative passive participle from H3618; bridehood (only in the plural): - espousal.
H3624: From an unused root meaning to be complete ; maturity: - full (old) age.
H3625: The same as H3624; Kelach, a place in Assyria: - Calah.
H3626: From H3605 and H2374; every seer ; Col-Cho-zeh, an Israelite: - Col-hozeh.
H3627: From H3615; something prepared, that is, any apparatus (as an implement, utensil, dress, vessel or weapon): - armour ([-bearer]), artillery, bag, carriage, + furnish, furniture, instrument, jewel, that is made of, X one from another, that which pertaineth, pot, + psaltery, sack, stuff, thing, tool, vessel, ware, weapon, + whatsoever.
H3628: From H3607 (compare H3608); a prison: - prison.
H3629: Feminine of H3627 (only in the plural); a kidney (as an essential organ); figuratively the mind (as the interior self): - kidneys, reins.
H3630: A form of H3631; Kiljon, an Israelite: - Chilion.
H3631: From H3615; pining, destruction: - consumption, failing.
H3632: From H3634; complete ; as noun, the whole (specifically a sacrifice entirely consumed); as adverb fully: - all, every whit, flame, perfect (-ion), utterly, whole burnt offering (sacrifice), wholly.
H3633: From H3557; sustenance ; Calcol, an Israelite: - Calcol, Chalcol.
H3634: A primitive root; to complete: - (make) perfect.

H3641: Of foreign derivation; Calneh or Calno, a place in the Assyrian empire: - Calneh, Calno. Compare H3656.

H3657: From H3661; a plant (as set): - X vineyard.

H3668: Feminine of H3667; Kenaanah, the name of two Israelites: - Chenaanah.

H3674: From H3655; a colleague (as having the same title): - companion.

H3682: From H3680; a cover (garment); figuratively a veiling: - covering, raiment, vesture.

H3691: Probably of foreign origin; Kisleu, the ninth Hebrew month: - Chisleu.
H3692: From H3688; hopeful ; Kislon, an Israelite: - Chislon.

H3695: A plural probably of foreign derivation; Casluchim, a people cognate to the Egyptian: - Casluhim.
H3696: From the feminine plural of H3689 and H8396; flanks of Tabor ; Kisloth Tabor, a place in Palestine: - Chisloth-tabor.

H3698: From H3697; spelt (from its bristliness as if just shorn): - fitches, rie.

H3710: From H3721; a hollow rock: - rock.
H3711: A primitive root; properly to bend, that is, (figuratively) to tame or subdue: - pacify.

H3728: A primitive root; to tread down; figuratively to humiliate: - cover.
H3729: (Chaldee); a root of uncertain correspondence; to fetter: - bind.

H3736: From the same as H3525; to gird or clothe: - clothed.
H3737: (Chaldee); from a verb corresponding to that of H3736; a mantle: - hat.
H3738: A primitive root; properly to dig ; figuratively to plot ; generally to bore or open: - dig, X make (a banquet), open.

H3741: Feminine of H3733; a meadow: - cottage.
H3742: Of uncertain derivation; a cherub or imaginary figure: - cherub, [plural] cherubims.

H3745: (Chaldee); probably of Greek origin [H2784]; to proclaim: - make a proclamation.

H3747: From H3772; a cut ; Kerith, a brook of Palestine: - Cherith.

H3750: Probably of foreign origin; the crocus: - saffron.
H3751: Of foreign derivation; Karkemish, a place in Syria: - Carchemish.

H3753: From H3769; a dromedary (from its rapid motion as if dancing): - swift beast.
H3754: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a garden or vineyard : - vines, (increase of the) vineyard (-s), vintage. See also H1021.

H3758: Probably of foreign origin; carmine, a deep red: - crimson.

H3763: Of uncertain derivation; Keran, an aboriginal Idumaean: - Cheran.
H3764: (Chaldee); corresponding to H3678; a throne: - throne.
H3765: From H3697; to lay waste: - waste.

H3777: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; Kesed, a relative of Abraham: - Chesed.

H3795: From H3807; beaten, that is, pure (oil): - beaten.
H3796: From an unused root meaning to compact ; a wall (as gathering inmates): - wall.

H3832: A primitive root; to overthrow ; intransitively to fall: - fall.
H3833: From an unused root meaning to roar ; a lion (properly a lioness as the fiercer (although not a roarer ; compare H738)): - (great, old, stout) lion, lioness, young [lion].
H3834: From H3823 in its original sense of fatness (or perhaps of folding); a cake (either as fried or turned): - cake.

H3850: From an unused root of uncertain signification; Lod, a place in Palestine: - Lod.

H4913: From H4861; Mashal, a place in Palestine: - Mashal.
H4915: (1) from H4910; empire ; (2) from H4911; a parallel: - dominion, like.

H4920: From H7999 and H3050; ally of Jah ; Meshelemjah, an Israelite: - Meshelemiah.
H4921: From H7999; reconciliation ; Meshillemith, an Israelite: - Meshillemith. Compare H4919.
H4922: Feminine of H4918; Meshullemeth, an Israelitess: - Meshullemeth.
H4923: From H8074; a waste or amazement: - astonishment, desolate.
H4924: From H8080; fat, that is, (literally and abstractly) fatness ; but usually (figuratively and concretely) a rich dish, a fertile field, a robust man: - fat (one, -ness, -test, -test place).
H4925: From H8080; fatness ; Mashmannah, an Israelite: - Mishmannah.
H4927: The same as H4926; Mishma, the name of a son of Ishmael, and of an Israelite: - Mishma.
H4928: Feminine of H4926; audience, that is, the royal court ; also obedience, that is, (concretely) a subject: - bidding, guard, obey.
H4929: From H8104; a guard (the man, the post, or the prison); figuratively a deposit ; also (as observed) a usage (abstractly), or an example (concretely): - diligence, guard, office, prison, ward, watch.
H4930: For H4548 feminine; a peg: - nail.
H4931: Feminine of H4929; watch, that is, the act (custody) or (concretely) the sentry, the post ; objectively preservation, or (concretely) safe ; figuratively observance, that is, (abstractly) duty, or (objectively) a usage or party: - charge, keep, to be kept, office, ordinance, safeguard, ward, watch.
H4932: From H8138; properly a repetition, that is, a duplicate (copy of a document), or a double (in amount); by implication a second (in order, rank, age, quality or location): - college, copy, double, fatlings, next, second (order), twice as much.
H4934: From the same as H8168; a hollow, that is, a narrow passage: - path.
H4935: Probably from H8159; inspection: - to supple.
H4936: Apparently from H8159; inspection ; Misham, an Israelite: - Misham.
H4937: From H8172; a support (concretely), that is, (figuratively) a protector or sustenance: - stay.

H4942: From H8192; a stall for cattle (only dual): - burden, sheepfold.
H4943: From an unused root meaning to hold ; possession: - + steward.
H4944: From H8264; a traversing, that is, rapid motion: - running to and fro.
H4945: From H8248; properly causing to drink, that is, a butler ; by implication (intransitively) drink (itself); figuratively a well watered region: - butler (-ship), cupbearer, drink (-ing), fat pasture, watered.

H4948: From H8254; weight (numerically estimated); hence, weighing (the act): - (full) weight.
H4949: Feminine of H4948 or H4947; a weight, that is, a plummet (with line attached): - plummet.
H4950: From H8257; a settling place (of water), that is, a pond: - deep.
H4952: From H8281 in the sense of loosening ; maceration, that is, steeped juice: - liquor.
H4953: (Chaldee); from a root corresponding to H8319; a (musical) pipe (from its whistling sound): - flute.
H4954: Patrial from an unused noun from an unused root; probably meaning to stretch out; extension ; a Mishraite, or inhabitant (collectively) of Mishra: - Mishraites.
H4955: From H8313; combustion, that is, cremation (of a corpse), or calcination (of lime): - burning.
H4956: From the plural of H4955 and H4325; burnings of water ; Misrephoth-Majim, a place in Palestine: - Misrephoth-mayim.
H4957: A form for H7796 used denominatively; vineyard ; Masrekah, a place in Idumaea: - Masrekah.
H4958: Apparently from an unused root meaning to perforate, that is, hollow out; a pan: - pan.
H4959: A primitive root; to feel of; by implication to grope: - feel, grope, search.
H4960: From H8354; drink ; by implication drinking (the act); also (by implication), a banquet or (generally) feast: - banquet, drank, drink, feast ([-ed], -ing).
H4961: (Chaldee); corresponding to H4960; a banquet: - banquet.

H4963: Denominative from H8401; straw in the heap: - straw.
H4964: From an unused root meaning to curb ; a bit: - bit, bridle.

H4980: The same as H4979; Mattanah, a place in the Desert: - Mattanah.
H4981: Probably patrial from an unused noun meaning slenderness ; a Mithnite, or inhabitant of Methen: - Mithnite.
H4982: From H4976; liberal ; Mattenai, the name of three Israelites: - Mattenai.
H4983: From H4976 and H3050; gift of Jah ; Mattanjah, the name of ten Israelites: - Mattaniah.
H4984: From H5375; (used as abstraction) supreme exaltation: - exalted.
H4985: A primitive root; to suck, by implication to relish, or (intransitively) be sweet: - be (made, X take) sweet.
H4986: From H4985; figuratively pleasantness (of discourse): - sweetness.
H4988: From H4985; a dainty, that is, (generally) food: - feed sweetly.
H4989: Feminine of H4987; sweetness ; Mithkah, a place in the Desert: - Mithcah.

H4992: For H4993; gift of Jah ; Mattattah, an Israelite: - Mattathah.
H4993: From H4991 and H3050; gift of Jah ; Mattithjah, the name of four Israelites: - Mattithiah.

H4995: Apparently from H5106 in the sense of harshness from refusal; properly tough, that is, uncooked (flesh): - raw.
H4996: Of Egyptian origin; no (that is, Thebes), the capital of Upper Egypt: - No. Compare H528.
H4997: From an unused root of uncertain signification; a (skin or leather) bag (for fluids): - bottle.

H4999: From H4998; a home ; figuratively a pasture: - habitation, house, pasture, pleasant place.
H5000: From H4998 or H5116; suitable, or beautiful: - becometh, comely, seemly.
H5001: A primitive root; properly to whisper, that is, (by implication) to utter as an oracle: - say.
H5002: From H5001; an oracle: - (hath) said, saith.
H5003: A primitive root; to commit adultery ; figuratively to apostatize: - adulterer (-ess), commit (-ing) adultery, woman that breaketh wedlock.
H5006: A primitive root; to scorn ; or (Ecc_12:5) by interchange for H5132, to bloom: - abhor, (give occasion to) blaspheme, contemn, despise, flourish, X great, provoke.
H5008: A primitive root; to groan: - groan.
H5010: A primitive root; to reject: - abhor, make void.
H5011: The same as H5108; fruit ; Nob, a place in Palestine: - Nob.
H5012: A primitive root; to prophesy, that is, speak (or sing) by inspiration (in prediction or simple discourse): - prophesy (-ing) make self a prophet.
H5014: A primitive root; to pierce ; to be hollow, or (figuratively) foolish: - hollow, vain.
H5015: Probably of foreign derivation; Nebo, the name of a Babylonian deity, also of a mountain in Moab, and of a place in Palestine: - Nebo.
H5016: From H5012; a prediction (spoken or written): - prophecy.
H5017: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5016; inspired teaching: - prophesying.

H5022: Feminine plural from the same as H5011; fruits ; Naboth, an Israelite: - Naboth.
H5023: (Chaldee); of uncertain derivation; a largess: - reward.
H5024: A primitive root; to bark (as a dog): - bark.

H5028: From H5027; regard ; Nebat, the father of Jeroboam (the first): - Nebat.

H5036: From H5034; stupid ; wicked (especially impious): - fool (-ish, -ish man, -ish woman), vile person.

H5044: Of uncertain derivation; Nibshan, a place in Palestine: - Nibshan.

H5061: From H5060; a blow (figuratively infliction); also (by implication) a spot (concretely a leprous person or dress): - plague, sore, stricken, stripe, stroke, wound.

H5075: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5074; to depart: - go from.
H5076: Passive participle of H5074; properly tossed ; abstractly a rolling (on the bed): - tossing to and fro.
H5077: A primitive root; properly to toss ; figuratively to exclude, that is, banish, postpone, prohibit: - cast out, drive, put far away.
H5078: From H5077 in the sense of freely flinging money; a bounty (for prostitution): - gifts.

H5083: Probably from an unused root meaning to give ; a present (for prostitution): - gift.
H5084: Of uncertain derivation; a sheath (of a sword): - sheath.

H5086: A primitive root; to shove asunder, that is, disperse: - drive (away, to and fro), thrust down, shaken, tossed to and fro.
H5087: A primitive root; to promise (positively, to do or give something to God): - (make a) vow.
H5088: From H5087; a promise (to God); also (concretely) a thing promised: - vow ([-ed]).
H5089: From an unused root meaning to lament ; lamentation: - wailing.

H5094: (Chaldee); from the same as H5105; illumination, that is, (figuratively) wisdom: - light.

H5098: A primitive root; to growl: - mourn, roar (-ing).
H5100: Feminine of H5099; snarling: - disquietness, roaring.
H5101: A primitive root; to bray (as an ass), scream (from hunger): - bray.

H5106: A primitive root; to refuse, forbid, dissuade, or neutralize: - break, disallow, discourage, make of none effect.

H5109: From H5108; fruitful ; Nobai, an Israelite: - Nebai [from the margin].

H5115: A primitive root; to rest (as at home); causatively (through the implied idea of beauty (compare H5116)), to celebrate (with praises): - keep at home, prepare an habitation.
H5116: From H5115; (adjective) at home ; hence (by implication of satisfaction) lovely ; also (noun) a home, of God (temple), men (residence), flocks (pasture), or wild animals (den): - comely, dwelling (place), fold, habitation, pleasant place, sheepcote, stable, tarried.
H5117: A primitive root; to rest, that is, settle down; used in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively, intransitively, transitively and causatively (to dwell, stay, let fall, place, let alone, withdraw, give comfort, etc.): - cease, be confederate, lay, let down, (be) quiet, remain, (cause to, be at, give, have, make to) rest, set down. Compare H3241.
H5119: Feminine of H5118; quietude ; Nochah, an Israelite: - Nohah.
H5121: From H5115; residence ; Navith, a place in Palestine: - Naioth [from the margin].
H5122: (Chaldee); from an unused root probably meaning to be foul ; a sink: - dunghill.
H5123: A primitive root; to slumber (from drowsiness): - sleep, slumber.
H5125: A primitive root; to resprout, that is, propagate by shoots; figuratively, to be perpetual: - be continued.
H5126: From H5125; perpetuity ; Nun or Non, the father of Joshua: - Non, Nun.
H5127: A primitive root; to flit, that is, vanish away (subside, escape; causatively chase, impel, deliver): - X abate, away, be displayed, (make to) flee (away, -ing), put to flight, X hide, lift up a standard.
H5128: A primitive root; to waver, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (as subjoined): - continually, fugitive, X make to [go] up and down, be gone away, (be) move (-able, -d), be promoted, reel, remove, scatter, set, shake, sift, stagger, to and fro, be vagabond, wag, (make) wander (up and down).
H5129: From H3259 and H3050; convened of Jah ; Noadjah, the name of an Israelite, and a false prophetess: - Noadiah.
H5130: A primitive root; to quiver (that is, vibrate up and down, or rock to and fro); used in a great variety of applications (including sprinkling, beckoning, rubbing, bastinadoing, sawing, waving, etc.): - lift up, move, offer, perfume, send, shake, sift, strike, wave.
H5131: From H5130; elevation : - situation. Compare H5297.
H5132: A primitive root; properly to flash ; hence, to blossom (from the brilliancy of color); also, to fly away (from the quickness of motion): - flee away, bud (forth).
H5133: Feminine active participle of H5327 in the sense of flying ; a pinion (or wing feather); often (collectively) plumage: - feather (-s), ostrich.
H5134: A primitive root; to suckle: - nurse.
H5135: (Chaldee); from an unused root (corresponding to that of H5216) meaning to shine ; fire: - fiery, fire.
H5136: A primitive root; to be sick, that is, (figuratively) distressed: - be full of heaviness.
H5137: A primitive root; to spirt, that is, besprinkle (especially in expiation): - sprinkle.
H5138: From H2102; something boiled, that is, soup: - pottage.
H5139: From H5144; separate, that is, consecrated (as prince, a Nazirite); hence (figuratively from the latter) an unpruned vine (like an unshorn Nazirite). (The translation, Nazarite, is by a false alliteration with Nazareth.): - Nazarite [by a false alliteration with Nazareth], separate (-d), vine undressed.
H5140: A primitive root; to drip, or shed by trickling: - distil, drop, flood, (cause to) flow (-ing), gush out, melt, pour (down), running water, stream.
H5141: From an unused root of uncertain meaning; a nose ring: - earring, jewel.
H5142: (Chaldee); corresponding to the root of H5143; to suffer (causatively inflict) loss: - have (en-) damage, hurt (-ful).
H5143: From an unused root meaning to injure ; loss: - damage.
H5144: A primitive root; to hold aloof, that is, (intransitively) abstain (from food and drink, from impurity, and even from divine worship (that is, apostatize)); specifically to set apart (to sacred purposes), that is, devote: - consecrate, separate (-ing, self).
H5145: From H5144; properly something set apart, that is, (abstractly) dedication (of a priest or Nazirite); hence (concretely) unshorn locks ; also (by implication) a chaplet (especially of royalty): - consecration, crown, hair, separation.
H5146: The same as H5118; rest ; Noach, the patriarch of the flood: - Noah.
H5147: From H2247; occult ; Nachbi, an Israelite: - Nakbi.
H5148: A primitive root; to guide ; by implication to transport (into exile, or as colonists): - bestow, bring, govern, guide, lead (forth), put, straiten.
H5149: From H5162; comforted ; Nechum, an Israelite: - Nehum.
H5150: From H5162; properly consoled ; abstractly solace: - comfort (-able), repenting.
H5151: From H5162; comfortable ; Nachum, an Israelitish prophet: - Nahum.
H5152: From the same as H5170; snorer ; Nachor, the name of the grandfather and a brother of Abraham: - Nahor.
H5153: Apparently passive participle of H5172 (perhaps in the sense of ringing, that is, bell metal; or from the red color of the throat of a serpent (H5175, as denominative) when hissing); coppery, that is, (figuratively) hard: - of brass.
H5154: Feminine of H5153; copper : - brass, steel. Compare H5176.
H5155: Probably denominative from H2485; a flute: - [plural] Nehiloth.
H5156: From the same as H5170; a nostril: - [dual] nostrils.
H5157: A primitive root; to inherit (as a (figurative) mode of descent), or (generally) to occupy ; causatively to bequeath, or (generally) distribute, instate: - divide, have ([inheritance]), take as an heritage, (cause to, give to, make to) inherit, (distribute for, divide [for, for an, by], give for, have, leave for, take [for]) inheritance, (have in, cause to be made to) possess (-ion).
H5158: From H5157 in its original sense; a stream, especially a winter torrent ; (by implication) a (narrow) valley (in which a brook runs); also a shaft (of a mine): - brook, flood, river, stream, valley.
H5159: From H5157 (in its usual sense); properly something inherited, that is, (abstractly) occupancy, or (concretely) an heirloom ; generally an estate, patrimony or portion : - heritage, to inherit, inheritance, possession. Compare H5158.
H5160: From H5158 and H410; valley of God ; Nachaliel, a place in the Desert: - Nahaliel.
H5161: Apparently a patronymic from an unused name (apparently passive participle of H2492); dreamed ; a Nechelamite, or descendant of Nechlam: - Nehelamite.
H5162: A primitive root; properly to sigh, that is, breathe strongly; by implication to be sorry, that is, (in a favorable sense) to pity, console or (reflexively) rue ; or (unfavorably) to avenge (oneself): - comfort (self), ease [one's self], repent (-er, -ing, self).
H5163: From H5162; consolation ; Nacham, an Israelite: - Naham.
H5164: From H5162; ruefulness, that is, desistance: - repentance.
H5166: From H5162 and H3050; consolation of Jah ; Nechemjah, the name of three Israelites: - Nehemiah.
H5167: From H5162; consolatory ; Nachamani, an Israelite: - Nahamani.
H5169: A primitive root; to be urgent: - require haste.
H5170: From an unused root meaning to snort or snore ; a snorting: - nostrils, snorting.
H5171: From the same as H5170; snorer ; Nacharai or Nachrai, an Israelite: - Naharai, Nahari.
H5172: A primitive root; properly to hiss, that is, whisper a (magic) spell; generally to prognosticate: - X certainly, divine, enchanter, (use) X enchantment, learn by experience, X indeed, diligently observe.
H5173: From H5172; an incantation or augury: - enchantment.
H5175: From H5172; a snake (from its hiss): - serpent.
H5176: The same as H5175; Nachash, the name of two persons apparently non Israelites: - Nahash.
H5177: From H5172; enchanter ; Nachshon, an Israelite: - Naashon, Nahshon.
H5178: For H5154; copper ; hence, something made of that metal, that is, coin, a fetter ; figuratively base (as compared with gold or silver): - brasen, brass, chain, copper, fetter (of brass), filthiness, steel.
H5179: From H5178; copper ; Nechushta, an Israelitess: - Nehushta.
H5180: From H5178; something made of copper, that is, the copper serpent of the Desert: - Nehushtan.
H5181: A primitive root; to sink, that is, descend ; causatively, to press or lead down: - be broken, (cause to) come down, enter, go down, press sore, settle, stick fast.
H5182: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5181; to descend ; causatively, to bring away, deposit, depose: - carry, come down, depose, lay up, place.
H5183: From H5182; a descent, that is, imposition, unfavorable (punishment) or favorable (food); also (intransitively; perhaps from H5117), restfulness: - lighting down, quiet (-ness), to rest, be set on.
H5184: The same as H5183; quiet ; Nachath, the name of an Edomite and of two Israelites: - Nahath.
H5186: A primitive root; to stretch or spread out; by implication to bend away (including moral deflection); used in a great variety of applications: - + afternoon, apply, bow (down, -ing), carry aside, decline, deliver, extend, go down, be gone, incline, intend, lay, let down, offer, outstretched, overthrown, pervert, pitch, prolong, put away, shew, spread (out), stretch (forth, out), take (aside), turn (aside, away), wrest, cause to yield.
H5188: From H5197; a pendant for the ears (especially of pearls): - chain, collar.
H5189: From H5203; a tendril (as an offshoot): - battlement, branch, plant.
H5190: A primitive root; to lift ; by implication to impose: - bear, offer, take up.
H5191: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5190; to raise: - take up.
H5193: A primitive root; properly to strike in, that is, fix ; specifically to plant (literally or figuratively): - fastened, plant (-er).
H5194: From H5193; a plant ; collectively, a plantation ; abstractly, a planting: - plant.
H5196: Plural of H5194; Netaim, a place in Palestine: - plants.
H5197: A primitive root; to ooze, that is, distil gradually; by implication to fall in drops ; figuratively to speak by inspiration: - drop (-ping), prophesy (-et).
H5198: From H5197; a drop ; specifically, an aromatic gum (probably stacte): - drop, stacte.
H5199: From H5197; distillation ; Netophah, a place in Palestine: - Netophah.
H5200: Patronymic from H5199; a Netophathite, or inhabitant of Netophah: - Netophathite.
H5201: A primitive root; to guard ; figuratively, to cherish (anger): - bear grudge, keep (-er), reserve.
H5202: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5201; to retain: - keep.
H5203: A primitive root; properly to pound, that is, smite ; by implication (as if beating out, and thus expanding) to disperse ; also, to thrust off, down, out or upon (including reject, let alone, permit, remit, etc.): - cast off, drawn, let fall, forsake, join [battle], leave (off), lie still, loose, spread (self) abroad, stretch out, suffer.
H5204: A doubtful word; apparently from H5091; lamentation: - wailing.
H5205: From H5110; motion (of the lips in speech): - moving.
H5206: Feminine of H5205; removal, that is, exile: - removed.
H5207: From H5117; properly restful, that is, pleasant ; abstractly delight: - sweet (odour).
H5208: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5207; pleasure: - sweet odour (savour).
H5210: Of foreign origin; Nineveh, the capital of Assyria: - Nineveh.
H5212: Probably of foreign origin; Nisan, the first month of the Jewish sacred year: - Nisan.
H5214: A root probably identical with that of H5216, through the idea of the gleam of a fresh furrow; to till the soil: - break up.
H5215: From H5214; properly ploughing, that is, (concretely) freshly ploughed land: - fallow ground, ploughing, tillage.
H5216: From a primitive root (see H5214 and H5135) properly meaning to glisten ; a lamp (that is, the burner) or light (literally or figuratively): - candle, lamp, light.
H5217: A primitive root; to smite, that is, drive away: - be viler.
H5218: From H5217; smitten, that is, (figuratively) afflicted: - broken, stricken, wounded.
H5219: From H5218; properly a smiting, that is, (concretely) an aromatic gum (perhaps styrax), (as powdered): - spicery (-ces).
H5220: From an unused root meaning to propagate ; offspring: - nephew, son's son.
H5221: A primitive root; to strike (lightly or severely, literally or figuratively): - beat, cast forth, clap, give [wounds], X go forward, X indeed, kill, make [slaughter], murderer, punish, slaughter, slay (-er, -ing), smite (-r, -ing), strike, be stricken, (give) stripes, X surely, wound.
H5222: From H5221; a smiter, that is, (figuratively) traducer: - abject.
H5223: smitten, that is, (literally) maimed, or (figuratively) dejected: - contrite, lame.
H5224: Probably of Egyptian origin; Neko an Egyptian king: - Necho. Compare H6549.
H5225: From H3559; prepared ; Nakon, probably an Israelite: - Nachon.
H5226: From an unused root meaning to be straightforward ; properly the fore part; used adverbially, opposite: - before, over against.
H5227: From the same as H5226; properly, the front part; used adverbially (especially with a preposition), opposite, in front of, forward, in behalf of: - (over) against, before, direct [-ly], for, right (on).
H5228: From the same as H5226; straightforward, that is, (figuratively), equitable, correct, or (abstractly), integrity: - plain, right, uprightness.
H5229: Feminine of H5228; properly straight forwardness, that is, (figuratively) integrity, or (concretely) a truth: - equity, right (thing), uprightness.
H5230: A primitive root; to defraud, that is, act treacherously: - beguile, conspire, deceiver, deal subtilly.
H5233: From an unused root meaning to accumulate ; treasure: - riches, wealth.
H5234: A primitive root; properly to scrutinize, that is, look intently at; hence (with recognition implied), to acknowledge, be acquainted with, care for, respect, revere, or (with suspicion implied), to disregard, ignore, be strange toward, reject, resign, dissimulate (as if ignorant or disowning): - acknowledge, X could, deliver, discern, dissemble, estrange, feign self to be another, know, take knowledge (notice), perceive, regard, (have) respect, behave (make) self strange (-ly).
H5235: From H5234; something strange, that is, unexpected calamity: - strange.
H5236: From H5234; foreign, or (concretely) a foreigner, or (abstractly) heathendom: - alien, strange (+ -er).
H5237: From H5235 (second form); strange, in a variety of degrees and applications (foreign, non-relative, adulterous, different, wonderful): - alien, foreigner, outlandish, strange (-r, woman).
H5238: Probably for H5219; spicery, that is, (generally) valuables: - precious things.
H5239: Apparently a primitive root; to complete: - make an end.
H5241: Apparently for H3223; Nemuel, the name of two Israelites: - Nemuel.
H5242: From H5241; a Nemuelite, or descendant of Nemuel: - Nemuelite.
H5243: A primitive root; to become clipped or (specifically) circumcised: - (branch to) be cut down (off), circumcise.
H5244: Feminine from H5243; an ant (probably from its almost bisected form): - ant.
H5246: From an unused root meaning properly to filtrate, that is, be limpid (compare H5247 and H5249); and thus to spot or stain as if by dripping; a leopard (from its stripes): - leopard.
H5247: From the same as H5246; clear water; Nimrah, a place East of the Jordan: - Nimrah. See also H1039, H5249.
H5248: Probably of foreign origin; Nimrod, a son of Cush: - Nimrod.
H5249: Plural of a masculine corresponding to H5247; clear waters; Nimrim, a place East of the Jordan: - Nimrim. Compare H1039.
H5250: Probably from H4871; extricated ; Nimshi, the (grand-) father of Jehu: - Nimshi.
H5251: From H5264; a flag ; also a sail ; by implication a flagstaff ; generally a signal ; figuratively a token: - banner, pole, sail, (en-) sign, standard.
H5252: Feminine participle passive of H5437; properly an environment, that is, circumstance or turn of affairs: - cause.
H5253: A primitive root; to retreat: - departing away, remove, take (hold), turn away.
H5254: A primitive root; to test ; by implication to attempt: - adventure, assay, prove, tempt, try.
H5255: A primitive root; to tear away: - destroy, pluck, root.
H5257: From H5258; properly something poured out, that is, a libation ; also a molten image ; by implication a prince (as anointed): - drink offering, duke, prince (-ipal).
H5258: A primitive root; to pour out, especially a libation, or to cast (metal); by analogy to anoint a king: - cover, melt, offer, (cause to) pour (out), set (up).
H5259: A primitive root (probably identical with H5258 through the idea of fusion); to interweave, that is, (figuratively) to overspread: - that is spread.
H5260: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5258; to pour out a libation: - offer.
H5261: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5262; a libation: - drink offering.
H5262: From H5258; a libation ; also a cast idol: - cover, drink offering, molten image.
H5263: A primitive root; to wane, that is, be sick.
H5264: A primitive root; to gleam from afar, that is, to be conspicuous as a signal; or rather perhaps a denominative from H5251 (and identical with H5263, through the idea of a flag as fluttering in the wind); to raise a beacon: - lift up as an ensign, standard bearer.
H5265: A primitive root; properly to pull up, especially the tent pins, that is, start on a journey: - cause to blow, bring, get, (make to) go (away, forth, forward, onward, out), (take) journey, march, remove, set aside (forward), X still, be on his (go their) way.
H5266: A primitive root; to go up: - ascend.
H5268: Of foreign origin; Nisrok, a Babylonian idol: - Nisroch.
H5269: From H5128; motion ; Neah, a place in Palestine: - Neah.
H5270: From H5128; movement ; Noah, an Israelitess: - Noah.
H5271: Properly passive participle from H5288 as denominative; (only in plural collectively or emphatically) youth, the state (juvenility) or the persons (young people): - childhood, youth.
H5272: From H5128 and H410; moved of God ; Neiel, a place in Palestine: - Neiel.
H5273: From H5276; delightful (objectively or subjectively, literally or figuratively): - pleasant (-ure), sweet.
H5274: A primitive root; properly to fasten up, that is, with a bar or cord; hence (denominatively from H5275), to sandal, that is, furnish with slippers: - bolt, inclose, lock, shod, shut up.
H5275: From H5274; properly a sandal tongue ; by extension a sandal or slipper (sometimes as a symbol of occupancy, a refusal to marry, or of something valueless): - dryshod, (pair of) shoe ([-latchet], -s).
H5276: A primitive root; to be agreeable (literally or figuratively): - pass in beauty, be delight, be pleasant, be sweet.
H5277: From H5276; pleasure ; Naam, an Israelite: - Naam.
H5278: From H5276; agreeableness, that is, delight, suitableness, splendor or grace: - beauty, pleasant (-ness).
H5279: Feminine of H5277; pleasantness ; Naamah, the name of an antediluvian woman, of an Ammonitess, and of a place in Palestine: - Naamah.
H5280: Patronymic from H5283; a Naamanite, or descendant of Naaman (collectively): - Naamites.
H5281: From H5278; pleasant ; Noomi, an Israelitess: - Naomi.
H5282: From H5276; pleasantness (plural as concrete): - pleasant.
H5283: The same as H5282; Naaman, the name of an Israelite and of a Damascene: - Naaman.
H5284: Patrial from a place corresponding in nmae (but not identical) with H5279; a Naamathite, or inhabitant of Naamah: - Naamathite
H5285: From an unused root meaning to prick ; probably a brier ; by implication a thicket of thorny bushes: - thorn.
H5286: A primitive root; to growl: - yell.
H5287: A primitive root (probably identical with H5286, through the idea of the rustling of mane, which usually accompanies the lion's roar); to tumble about: - shake (off, out, self), overthrow, toss up and down.
H5288: From H5287; (concretely) a boy (as active), from the age of infancy to adolescence; by implication a servant ; also (by interchange of sex), a girl (of similar latitude in age): - babe, boy, child, damsel [from the margin], lad, servant, young (man).
H5289: From H5287 in its derived sense of tossing about; a wanderer: - young one.
H5290: From H5287; (abstractly) boyhood (compare H5288): - child, youth.
H5291: Feminine of H5288; a girl (from infancy to adolescence): - damsel, maid (-en), young (woman).
H5292: The same as H5291; Naarah, the name of an Israelitess, and of a place in Palestine: - Naarah, Naarath.
H5293: From H5288; youthful ; Naarai, an Israelite: - Naarai.
H5294: From H5288 and H3050; servant of Jah ; Nearjah, the name of two Israelites: - Neariah.
H5295: From H5288; juvenile ; Naaran, a place in Palestine: - Naaran.
H5296: From H5287; something shaken out, that is, tow (as the refuse of flax): - tow.
H5297: A variation of H4644; Noph, the capital of Upper Egypt: - Noph.
H5298: From an unused root probably meaning to spring forth; a sprout ; Nepheg, the name of two Israelites: - Nepheg.
H5299: From H5130 in the sense of lifting ; a height ; also a sieve: - border, coast, region, sieve.
H5300: For H5304; Nephushesim, a Temple Servant: - Nephisesim [from the margin].
H5301: A primitive root; to puff, in various applications (literally, to inflate, blow hard, scatter, kindle, expire ; figuratively, to disesteem): - blow, breath, give up, cause to lose [life], seething, snuff.
H5302: From H5301; a gust ; Nophach, a place in Moab: - Nophah.
H5303: From H5307; properly, a feller, that is, a bully or tyrant: - giant.
H5304: Plural from an unused root meaning to scatter ; expansions ; Nephisim, a Temple Servant: - Nephusim [from the margin].
H5305: From H5314; refreshed ; Naphish, a son of Ishmael, and his posterity: - Naphish.
H5306: From an unused root meaning to glisten ; shining ; a gem, probably the garnet: - emerald.
H5307: A primitive root; to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitively or causatively, literally or figuratively): - be accepted, cast (down, self, [lots], out), cease, die, divide (by lot), (let) fail, (cause to, let, make, ready to) fall (away, down, -en, -ing), fell (-ing), fugitive, have [inheritamce], inferior, be judged [by mistake for H6419], lay (along), (cause to) lie down, light (down), be (X hast) lost, lying, overthrow, overwhelm, perish, present (-ed, -ing), (make to) rot, slay, smite out, X surely, throw down.
H5308: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5307: - fall (down), have occasion.
H5309: From H5307; something fallen, that is, an abortion: - untimely birth.
H5310: A primitive root; to dash to pieces, or scatter: - be beaten in sunder, break (in pieces), broken, dash (in pieces), cause to be discharged, dispersed, be overspread, scatter.
H5311: From H5310; a storm (as dispersing): - scattering.
H5312: (Chaldee); a primitive root; to issue ; causatively, to bring out: - come (go, take) forth (out).
H5313: (Chaldee); from H5312; an outgo, that is, expense: - expense.
H5314: A primitive root; to breathe ; passively, to be breathed upon, that is, (figuratively) refreshed (as if by a current of air): - (be) refresh selves (-ed).
H5315: From H5314; properly a breathing creature, that is, animal or (abstractly) vitality ; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental): - any, appetite, beast, body, breath, creature, X dead (-ly), desire, X [dis-] contented, X fish, ghost, + greedy, he, heart (-y), (hath, X jeopardy of) life (X in jeopardy), lust, man, me, mind, mortality, one, own, person, pleasure, (her-, him-, my-, thy-) self, them (your) -selves, + slay, soul, + tablet, they, thing, (X she) will, X would have it.
H5317: From H5130 in the sense of shaking to pieces; a dripping that is, of honey (from the comb): - honeycomb.
H5318: From H6605; opened, that is, a spring ; Nephtoach, a place in Palestine: - Neptoah.
H5319: From H6617; properly wrestled ; but used (in the plural) transitively, a struggle: - wrestling.
H5320: Plural of foreign origin; Naphtuchim, an Egyptian tribe: - Naptuhim.
H5321: From H6617; my wrestling ; Naphtali, a son of Jacob, with the tribe descended from him, and its territory: - Naphtali.
H5322: From H5340; a flower (from its brilliancy); also a hawk (from its flashing speed): - blossom, hawk.
H5323: A primitive root; to go away: - flee.
H5324: A primitive root; to station, in various applications (literally or figuratively): - appointed, deputy, erect, establish, X Huzzah [by mistake for a proper name], lay, officer, pillar, present, rear up, set (over, up), settle, sharpen, stablish, (make to) stand (-ing, still, up, upright), best state.
H5325: Passive participle of H5324; fixed, that is, a handle: - haft.
H5326: (Chaldee); from a root corresponding to H5324; fixedness, that is, firmness: - strength.
H5327: A primitive root; properly to go forth, that is, (by implication) to be expelled, and (consequently) desolate ; causatively to lay waste ; also (specifically), to quarrel: - be laid waste, ruinous, strive (together).
H5328: Feminine of H5322; a blossom: - flower.
H5329: A primitive root; properly to glitter from afar, that is, to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); also (as denominative from H5331), to be permanent: - excel, chief musician (singer), oversee (-r), set forward.
H5330: (Chaldee); corresponding to H5329; to become chief: - be preferred.
H5331: From H5329; properly a goal, that is, the bright object at a distance travelled towards; hence (figuratively), splendor, or (subjectively) truthfulness, or (objectively) confidence ; but usually (adverbially), continually (that is, to the most distant point of view): - alway (-s), constantly, end, (+ n-) ever (more), perpetual, strength, victory.
H5332: Probably identical with H5331, through the idea of brilliancy of color; juice of the grape (as blood red): - blood, strength.
H5333: From H5324; something stationary, that is, a prefect, a military post, a statue: - garrison, officer, pillar.
H5334: The same as H5333; station ; Netsib, a place in Palestine: - Nezib.
H5335: From H5329; conspicuous ; Netsiach, a Temple Servant: - Neziah.

G5898: Humility, Gentleness. See Definition for tapeinophrosyne G5012

tapeinophrosyne is humility, not the making of one's self small when he is really great, but thinking little of one's self, because this is in a sense the right estimate for any human being, however great.

praotes is founded upon this idea, and goes beyond it. It is the attitude of mind and behavior which, arising from humility, disposes one to receive with gentleness and meekness whatever may come to him from others or from God.

Both words may be translated gentleness, yet there are marked differences in meaning. praotes is rather passive, denoting, as has been said above (see Humility, Gentleness), one's attitude toward others in view of their acts, bad or good.

epieikeia is distinctly active, it is seen in one's deeds toward others, and it usually implies the relation of superior to inferior. It is fundamentally a relaxing of strict legal requirements concerning others, yet doing this in order more fully to carry out the real spirit of the law. It is clemency in which there is no element of weakness or injustice.
G5906: Desire, Lust. See Definition for epithymia G1939
G5907: Affliction. See Definition for thlip'sis G2347
thlip'sis according to its derivation means pressure. In its figurative sense it is that which presses upon the spirit, affliction.

G5908: Bad, Evil. See Definition for kakos G2556

These words may be used with very little distinction of meaning, but often the difference is marked. kakos frequently means evil rather negatively, referring to the absence of the qualities which constitute a person or thing what it should be or what it claims to be. It is also used meaning evil in a moral sense. It is a general antithesis to agathos.
G5909: Punishment. See Definition for timoria G5098
timoria in classical and N.T. usage denotes especially the vindicative character of punishment, it is the punishment in relation to the punisher.

kolasis in classical Greek meant usually punishment which aimed at the reformation of the offender. But sometimes in later Greek, and always in the N.T., the idea of reformation seems to disappear, so that there remains simply the idea of punishment, but viewed in relation to the punished.
G5910: To pollute. See Definition for miaino G3392
miaino meant originally to stain, as with color.

molyno meant originally to smear over, as with mud or filth, always having a bad meaning, while the meaning of miaino might be either good or bad. According to classical Greek, miaino has a religious meaning, to profane, while molyno is simply to spoil, disgrace. As ethically applied in the N.T. they have both practically the same meaning, to pollute, defile. It is, however, true that miaino, to judge from classical usage, refers chiefly to the effect of the act not on the individual, but on others, on the community.
G5911: To do. See Definition for poieo G4160

G5915: To will, to Wish. See Definition for boulomai G1014

airesis is rather the separating tendency, so it is really more fundamental than schisma.

nous is distinctly the reflective consciousness, ``the organ of moral thinking and knowing, the intellectual organ of moral sentiment'' (Cremer).

nomos is the common word meaning law. It may mean law in general. In the N.T., however, it usually means the law of God, and most frequently the Mosaic law.

typos has many meanings, among the most common being image, pattern or model, and type. In the last sense it means a person or thing prefiguring a future person or thing, e.g., Adam as a type of Christ, Ro 5:14.

Both words in a certain sense mean rest, but from different standpoints. anapausis is rest which comes by cessation from labor, which may be simply temporary.

G5923: Wind. See Definition for pneuma G4151
G5924: Old. See Definition for palaios G3820

austeros has not necessarily an unfavorable meaning. It is well represented by the word austere? it means one who is earnest and severe, strict in his ways, opposed to all levity. By implication it may have the unfavorable meaning of harshness or morosene

G5933: Form, Appearance. See Definition for idea G2397
G5934: Clothing. See Definition for imation G2440

mochthos is labor, hard and often painful. It is the ordinary word for common labor which is the usual lot of humanity.

These words form a series. phyle is sometimes a race, nation, but usually a tribe, such as one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from the twelve sons of Jacob.
